    P8.5Code

    Elevator.java: two stop sets and LOOK
    /** One car running LOOK: keep going while there are stops ahead, then reverse. Not thread-safe: the controller owns it. */
class Elevator {
    final String id;
    private final int minFloor, maxFloor;
    private int floor;
    private Direction dir = Direction.IDLE;
    private final TreeSet<Integer> upStops = new TreeSet<>();     // pick-ups going up, and drop-offs above while going up
    private final TreeSet<Integer> downStops = new TreeSet<>();

    Elevator(String id, int startFloor, int minFloor, int maxFloor) {
        this.id = id; this.floor = startFloor; this.minFloor = minFloor; this.maxFloor = maxFloor;
    }

    /** `wanted` is the direction the passenger travels from `stop`. */
    void addStop(int stop, Direction wanted) {
        if (stop < minFloor || stop > maxFloor) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no floor " + stop);
        (wanted == Direction.DOWN ? downStops : upStops).add(stop);
    }

    /** A button inside the car: the direction follows from where the car is. */
    void pressInside(int target) {
        if (target != floor) addStop(target, target > floor ? Direction.UP : Direction.DOWN);
    }

    /** Advance one tick: open doors here, or move one floor. Returns an event for the log, or null. */
    String step() {
        if (upStops.isEmpty() && downStops.isEmpty()) { dir = Direction.IDLE; return null; }
        if (dir == Direction.IDLE) dir = towardNearest();
        if (serveHere()) return id + " doors open at " + floor;
        if (!stopsAhead()) {                                        // LOOK: nothing further this way, so turn around
            dir = dir == Direction.UP ? Direction.DOWN : Direction.UP;
            if (serveHere()) return id + " turns, doors open at " + floor;
        }
        floor += dir == Direction.UP ? 1 : -1;
        return null;
    }

    private boolean serveHere() {
        boolean served = (dir == Direction.UP ? upStops : downStops).remove(floor);
        if (!served && !stopsAhead()) served = (dir == Direction.UP ? downStops : upStops).remove(floor);   // last stop this way
        return served;
    }

    private boolean stopsAhead() {
        return dir == Direction.UP
                ? upStops.higher(floor) != null || downStops.higher(floor) != null
                : upStops.lower(floor) != null || downStops.lower(floor) != null;
    }

    private Direction towardNearest() {
        int best = Integer.MAX_VALUE, target = floor;
        for (TreeSet<Integer> s : List.of(upStops, downStops))
            for (int f : s) if (Math.abs(f - floor) < best) { best = Math.abs(f - floor); target = f; }
        if (target > floor) return Direction.UP;
        if (target < floor) return Direction.DOWN;
        return upStops.contains(floor) ? Direction.UP : Direction.DOWN;
    }

    int floor() { return floor; }
    Direction direction() { return dir; }
    boolean idle() { return upStops.isEmpty() && downStops.isEmpty(); }

    /** Farthest stop in the current direction: where the car will turn around. */
    int turnaround() {
        if (dir == Direction.UP) return Math.max(upStops.isEmpty() ? floor : upStops.last(), downStops.isEmpty() ? floor : downStops.last());
        if (dir == Direction.DOWN) return Math.min(upStops.isEmpty() ? floor : upStops.first(), downStops.isEmpty() ? floor : downStops.first());
        return floor;
    }
}
    NearestCarStrategy.java
    /** Estimated floors travelled before reaching the caller; ties go to the earlier car. */
class NearestCarStrategy implements DispatchStrategy {
    public Elevator choose(List<Elevator> cars, int floor, Direction wanted) {
        return cars.stream().min(Comparator.comparingInt(c -> cost(c, floor, wanted))).orElseThrow();
    }

    static int cost(Elevator c, int floor, Direction wanted) {
        int here = c.floor();
        if (c.idle()) return Math.abs(here - floor);
        boolean onTheWay = (c.direction() == Direction.UP && wanted == Direction.UP && floor >= here)
                || (c.direction() == Direction.DOWN && wanted == Direction.DOWN && floor <= here);
        if (onTheWay) return Math.abs(floor - here);
        int turn = c.turnaround();                              // finish this sweep, then come back
        return Math.abs(turn - here) + Math.abs(turn - floor);
    }
}
    ElevatorSystem.java: single-writer controller with a command inbox
    /** Single-writer controller: buttons enqueue commands from any thread; only step() touches the cars. */
class ElevatorSystem {
    private final Map<String, Elevator> cars = new LinkedHashMap<>();
    private final DispatchStrategy dispatch;
    private final Queue<Runnable> inbox = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();
    private final List<String> log = new ArrayList<>();
    private int tick = 0;

    ElevatorSystem(List<Elevator> cars, DispatchStrategy dispatch) {
        cars.forEach(c -> this.cars.put(c.id, c));
        this.dispatch = dispatch;
    }

    /** Hall button: safe from any thread. */
    void call(int floor, Direction wanted) {
        inbox.add(() -> {
            Elevator c = dispatch.choose(new ArrayList<>(cars.values()), floor, wanted);
            c.addStop(floor, wanted);
            log.add("t" + tick + ": call " + floor + " " + wanted + " -> car " + c.id);
        });
    }

    /** Car button: safe from any thread. */
    void press(String carId, int floor) {
        inbox.add(() -> cars.get(carId).pressInside(floor));
    }

    /** One tick of the simulation, run by the controller thread. */
    void step() {
        for (Runnable cmd; (cmd = inbox.poll()) != null; ) cmd.run();
        for (Elevator c : cars.values()) {
            String e = c.step();
            if (e != null) log.add("t" + tick + ": " + e);
        }
        tick++;
    }

    boolean allIdle() { return inbox.isEmpty() && cars.values().stream().allMatch(Elevator::idle); }
    List<String> log() { return log; }
    Elevator car(String id) { return cars.get(id); }
}

    Demo.java (complete)
    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Elevator a = new Elevator("A", 0, 0, 9), b = new Elevator("B", 9, 0, 9);
        ElevatorSystem sys = new ElevatorSystem(List.of(a, b), new NearestCarStrategy());
        sys.call(3, Direction.UP);              // A is 3 floors away, B is 6
        sys.step();
        sys.step();
        sys.call(7, Direction.DOWN);            // B (idle at 9) is closer than A (going up, then back)
        for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++) sys.step();
        sys.press("A", 6);                      // passenger boarded A at 3, going to 6
        sys.press("B", 1);                      // passenger boarded B at 7, going to 1
        while (!sys.allIdle()) sys.step();
        sys.log().forEach(System.out::println);
        System.out.println("final: A at " + a.floor() + ", B at " + b.floor());
        check(a.floor() == 6 && b.floor() == 1, "final floors");

        // LOOK: a car going up keeps going up before serving a call behind it
        Elevator c = new Elevator("C", 4, 0, 9);
        c.pressInside(8);
        c.step();                               // now moving up, at floor 5
        c.addStop(2, Direction.UP);             // a call below, wanting to go up
        StringBuilder path = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < 20 && !c.idle(); i++) { String e = c.step(); if (e != null) path.append(e.substring(2)).append("; "); }
        System.out.println("LOOK order: " + path);
        check(path.toString().indexOf("8") < path.toString().indexOf("2"), "serves 8 before 2");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P8.6Concurrency

    Buttons are pressed from many threads, but the car logic is not thread-safe, on purpose. Instead of locking every car method, the controller uses the single-writer principle: call and press only add a command to a ConcurrentLinkedQueue; one controller thread drains the queue at the start of each tick and is the only thread that touches cars. This removes races by construction, keeps the car code simple, and makes the order of events deterministic.

    The alternative, a lock per car plus a lock for dispatch decisions, works but must take care: dispatch reads every car's state, so it needs a consistent snapshot, and lock ordering between cars matters if one operation touches two cars.

    In production

    Real controllers are event-driven embedded systems, with safety interlocks in hardware. The software pattern above (one event loop that owns state, fed by a queue) is also how actor systems, Redis, and Node.js avoid locks.

    P8.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Destination dispatch

      Passengers enter their destination in the lobby instead of pressing up or down.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      The hall call now carries a destination, so the dispatcher can group passengers going to nearby floors into the same car. The cost function changes (stops added to the car's route, not just distance); the Elevator gets both the pick-up and the drop-off at once. A new DispatchStrategy implementation; the car is unchanged.

    2. 2
      Weight limit

      A full car should not stop for more pick-ups.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Track load (sensor input) on the car. When full, the car skips hall pick-ups but still serves drop-offs; the dispatcher reassigns skipped hall calls to another car. The skip is a guard on serving an up or down hall stop, not on car stops.

    3. 3
      Peak hours

      Morning traffic is mostly lobby to upper floors.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Swap the strategy by time of day: an up-peak strategy parks idle cars at the lobby and assigns them in rotation. Strategies selected by a schedule are the strategy plus factory pattern from Module 6.

    4. 4
      A car breaks down

      What happens to its pending stops?

      Write your answer, then reveal

      The car moves to OutOfService (after stopping at the nearest floor). Its hall calls are re-dispatched to other cars; its car calls belong to passengers inside, who are handled by safety procedures. Dispatch skips out-of-service cars.

    P8.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: LOOK with direction-aware hall calls; pluggable dispatch with a sensible cost; a clear state diagram; a concurrency answer.

    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why keep separate up and down stop sets instead of one?
      Reveal

      A hall call carries the passenger's direction. A car going up should stop for "going up" calls on the way but not for "going down" calls, which it serves on the way back. One set loses that information.

    2. What is the difference between SCAN and LOOK?
      Reveal

      SCAN travels to the end of the shaft before reversing; LOOK reverses at the last requested floor in the current direction. LOOK wastes fewer trips.

    3. Why not run each car on its own thread?
      Reveal

      You can, but then dispatch reads cars that other threads are changing, which needs locks and consistent snapshots. One controller thread with a queue is simpler and deterministic; scale it by giving each bank of elevators its own controller.

    4. How do you test that a car never overshoots?
      Reveal

      Drive the simulation with scripted calls and assert after every tick that each car's floor stays within bounds and that each requested stop appears in the log exactly once.

    BookMyShow in LLD form. The modeling insight is that seat availability belongs to a show, not to a seat; the concurrency insight is an all-or-nothing hold on several seats with locks taken in a fixed order; the money insight is that payment happens between hold and confirm, so confirmation must re-check the hold.

    Try it first60 minutes

    Design movie ticket booking: cities, theatres, screens, movies, shows; a user picks seats on a seat map, holds them for 10 minutes while paying, then confirms. Two users must never get the same seat. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Theatre, Screen, Seat (physical) vs Show and ShowSeat (per-show status); seat states AVAILABLE, HELD, BOOKED with an expiry on holds; hold(show, seats) that locks the requested seats in sorted order and holds all or none; lazy expiry so stuck holds free themselves; confirm(hold, payment) that succeeds only if the same hold still owns every seat, otherwise refunds; pricing per seat category per show; and a plan for the database version (conditional updates, unique constraints).

    P9.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Catalog? Cities, theatres, screens, movies, shows (movie + screen + start time)
    Seat map? Seats with a category (silver, gold, recliner); price per category per show
    Booking flow? Select seats, hold for 10 minutes, pay, confirm
    Limits? 1 to 10 seats per booking
    Concurrency? Many users on the same show at once; no seat sold twice
    Payment? External; we receive a payment reference or a failure

    Invariants: a show seat is held by at most one hold and booked by at most one booking; a hold covers all its seats or none; a booking only confirms seats its hold still owns.

    P9.2Entities and responsibilities

    Class Responsibility
    Theatre, Screen, Seat Physical layout; a seat has an ID and a category
    Movie (record) Title, runtime
    Show Movie on a screen at a time; prices; one ShowSeat per seat
    ShowSeat Status for this show, hold ID and expiry, and its lock
    Hold (record) Seats, amount, expiry, user
    Booking (record) Confirmed seats, amount, payment reference
    BookingService Hold, confirm, cancel; enforces the invariants

    The key move, from Module 8: Seat is the type (it exists every day), ShowSeat is the instance with state (it exists per show). Putting a status on Seat breaks the moment a screen runs two shows.

    The code below leaves Theatre and Screen as plain containers and passes a screen as its list of seats: they matter for search and the seat map, but they carry no rules in the booking flow, so they are the first thing to cut in a time box.

    P9.3Class diagram

    P9.4Key flows

    P9.5Code

    ShowSeat.java: per-show status with lazy expiry
    /** One seat for one show: the unit of contention. Callers lock it before reading or changing status. */
class ShowSeat {
    final String seatId;
    final SeatCategory category;
    final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private SeatStatus status = SeatStatus.AVAILABLE;
    private String holdId;
    private Instant holdExpiresAt;

    ShowSeat(Seat seat) { this.seatId = seat.id(); this.category = seat.category(); }

    /** Available, or held by a hold that has expired (lazy expiry: no sweeper needed for correctness). */
    boolean isFree(Instant now) {
        return status == SeatStatus.AVAILABLE || (status == SeatStatus.HELD && !now.isBefore(holdExpiresAt));
    }

    void hold(String holdId, Instant until) {
        status = SeatStatus.HELD;
        this.holdId = holdId;
        this.holdExpiresAt = until;
    }

    boolean isHeldBy(String holdId, Instant now) {
        return status == SeatStatus.HELD && holdId.equals(this.holdId) && now.isBefore(holdExpiresAt);
    }

    void book() {
        status = SeatStatus.BOOKED;
        holdId = null;
        holdExpiresAt = null;
    }

    void release(String holdId) {
        if (status == SeatStatus.HELD && holdId.equals(this.holdId)) {
            status = SeatStatus.AVAILABLE;
            this.holdId = null;
            holdExpiresAt = null;
        }
    }

    SeatStatus status() { return status; }
}
    BookingService.java: ordered locks, all-or-nothing hold, confirm re-checks
    class BookingService {
    private static final Duration HOLD_FOR = Duration.ofMinutes(10);
    private final Map<String, Show> shows = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Hold> holds = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Booking> bookings = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final AtomicLong holdSeq = new AtomicLong(1), bookingSeq = new AtomicLong(1);

    void addShow(Show s) { shows.put(s.id, s); }

    /** All-or-nothing hold on several seats. Locks are taken in seat-id order, so two holds never deadlock. */
    Hold hold(String showId, String userId, List<String> seatIds, Instant now) {
        if (seatIds.isEmpty() || seatIds.size() > 10) throw new BookingException("choose 1 to 10 seats");
        Show show = show(showId);
        List<ShowSeat> seats = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String id : new TreeSet<>(seatIds)) seats.add(show.seat(id));          // sorted, de-duplicated
        lockAll(seats);
        try {
            for (ShowSeat s : seats)
                if (!s.isFree(now)) throw new BookingException("seat " + s.seatId + " is not available");
            String holdId = "H" + holdSeq.getAndIncrement();
            Instant until = now.plus(HOLD_FOR);
            long amount = 0;
            for (ShowSeat s : seats) { s.hold(holdId, until); amount += show.price(s.category); }
            Hold h = new Hold(holdId, showId, userId, seats.stream().map(s -> s.seatId).toList(), amount, until);
            holds.put(holdId, h);
            return h;
        } finally {
            unlockAll(seats);
        }
    }

    /** Called after payment succeeds. Fails if the hold expired: a late payment is refunded, even if the seats are still free. */
    Booking confirm(String holdId, String paymentRef, Instant now) {
        Hold h = holds.get(holdId);
        if (h == null) throw new BookingException("unknown hold " + holdId);
        Show show = show(h.showId());
        List<ShowSeat> seats = h.seatIds().stream().map(show::seat).toList();        // already in sorted order
        lockAll(seats);
        try {
            for (ShowSeat s : seats)
                if (!s.isHeldBy(holdId, now)) {
                    holds.remove(holdId);                                                  // a dead hold is never confirmable
                    throw new BookingException("hold " + holdId + " expired; refund " + paymentRef);
                }
            seats.forEach(ShowSeat::book);
            holds.remove(holdId);
            Booking b = new Booking("B" + bookingSeq.getAndIncrement(), h.showId(), h.userId(), h.seatIds(), h.amountPaise(), paymentRef);
            bookings.put(b.id(), b);
            return b;
        } finally {
            unlockAll(seats);
        }
    }

    /** Seat map counts for display; expired holds count as available. */
    int count(String showId, SeatStatus status, Instant now) { return show(showId).count(status, now); }

    void cancelHold(String holdId) {
        Hold h = holds.remove(holdId);
        if (h == null) return;
        List<ShowSeat> seats = h.seatIds().stream().map(show(h.showId())::seat).toList();
        lockAll(seats);
        try { seats.forEach(s -> s.release(holdId)); } finally { unlockAll(seats); }
    }

    private static void lockAll(List<ShowSeat> seats) { seats.forEach(s -> s.lock.lock()); }

    private static void unlockAll(List<ShowSeat> seats) {
        for (int i = seats.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) seats.get(i).lock.unlock();
    }

    private Show show(String id) {
        Show s = shows.get(id);
        if (s == null) throw new BookingException("unknown show " + id);
        return s;
    }
}

    Show.java
    import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.LinkedHashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

class Show {
    final String id;
    final Movie movie;
    final Instant start;
    private final Map<SeatCategory, Long> pricePaise;
    private final Map<String, ShowSeat> seats = new LinkedHashMap<>();

    Show(String id, Movie movie, Instant start, List<Seat> screenSeats, Map<SeatCategory, Long> prices) {
        this.id = id;
        this.movie = movie;
        this.start = start;
        this.pricePaise = new EnumMap<>(prices);
        for (Seat s : screenSeats) seats.put(s.id(), new ShowSeat(s));   // seat state is per show
    }

    ShowSeat seat(String seatId) {
        ShowSeat s = seats.get(seatId);
        if (s == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no seat " + seatId + " in show " + id);
        return s;
    }

    long price(SeatCategory c) { return pricePaise.get(c); }
    int count(SeatStatus st, Instant now) {
        int n = 0;
        for (ShowSeat s : seats.values()) {
            s.lock.lock();
            try {
                SeatStatus eff = s.isFree(now) ? SeatStatus.AVAILABLE : s.status();
                if (eff == st) n++;
            } finally { s.lock.unlock(); }
        }
        return n;
    }
}

    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        List<Seat> screen = new ArrayList<>();
        for (char row = 'A'; row <= 'B'; row++)
            for (int n = 1; n <= 10; n++) screen.add(new Seat("" + row + n, row == 'A' ? SeatCategory.SILVER : SeatCategory.GOLD));
        Map<SeatCategory, Long> prices = new EnumMap<>(Map.of(SeatCategory.SILVER, 20_000L, SeatCategory.GOLD, 35_000L, SeatCategory.RECLINER, 60_000L));
        Movie movie = new Movie("M1", "Interstellar", 169);
        Instant t0 = Instant.parse("2026-10-21T12:00:00Z");
        BookingService svc = new BookingService();
        svc.addShow(new Show("S1", movie, t0.plus(Duration.ofHours(6)), screen, prices));

        Hold asha = svc.hold("S1", "asha", List.of("B5", "B6"), t0);
        System.out.println("asha holds " + asha.seatIds() + " for " + asha.amountPaise() / 100 + " rupees until " + asha.expiresAt());
        try {
            svc.hold("S1", "ravi", List.of("B6", "B7"), t0.plusSeconds(60));        // B6 is held
        } catch (BookingException e) {
            System.out.println("ravi: " + e.getMessage());
        }
        Booking b = svc.confirm(asha.id(), "pay_123", t0.plusSeconds(240));         // paid within 10 minutes
        System.out.println("booked " + b.id() + " " + b.seatIds());

        Hold meera = svc.hold("S1", "meera", List.of("A1"), t0);
        Hold kabir = svc.hold("S1", "kabir", List.of("A1"), t0.plusSeconds(11 * 60));   // meera's hold expired
        System.out.println("kabir got A1 after meera's hold expired: " + kabir.seatIds());
        try {
            svc.confirm(meera.id(), "pay_456", t0.plusSeconds(12 * 60));
        } catch (BookingException e) {
            System.out.println("meera: " + e.getMessage());
        }
        check(b.seatIds().equals(List.of("B5", "B6")), "booking");
        Instant later = t0.plusSeconds(12 * 60);
        System.out.println("seat map S1: " + svc.count("S1", SeatStatus.AVAILABLE, later) + " available, "
                + svc.count("S1", SeatStatus.HELD, later) + " held, " + svc.count("S1", SeatStatus.BOOKED, later) + " booked");
        check(svc.count("S1", SeatStatus.HELD, later) == 1 && svc.count("S1", SeatStatus.BOOKED, later) == 2, "seat map");

        // 200 users race for random pairs of 20 seats on a new show: no seat is ever held twice
        svc.addShow(new Show("S2", movie, t0.plus(Duration.ofHours(9)), screen, prices));
        Set<String> taken = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
        CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16);
        for (int u = 0; u < 200; u++) {
            String user = "u" + u;
            pool.submit(() -> {
                ThreadLocalRandom r = ThreadLocalRandom.current();
                String s1 = screen.get(r.nextInt(20)).id(), s2 = screen.get(r.nextInt(20)).id();
                try { go.await(); } catch (InterruptedException e) { return; }
                try {
                    Hold h = svc.hold("S2", user, List.of(s1, s2), t0);
                    for (String s : h.seatIds()) check(taken.add(s), "seat held twice: " + s);
                    svc.confirm(h.id(), "pay-" + user, t0.plusSeconds(30));
                } catch (BookingException ignored) { /* lost the race: normal */ }
            });
        }
        go.countDown();
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "finished");
        check(taken.size() <= 20, "seats");
        System.out.println("race on S2: 200 users, no seat held or sold twice");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P9.6Concurrency

    Decision Why
    Lock per ShowSeat Users on different seats never wait for each other
    Lock seats in sorted ID order Two users holding overlapping sets (B6, B7 and B7, B6) cannot deadlock
    Check all, then change all, under the locks All-or-nothing: no partial holds to clean up
    Lazy expiry checked under the lock A stale hold never blocks a seat, with no sweeper race
    confirm re-checks ownership Payment can finish after the hold expired and another user took the seat

    A single lock per show would also be correct and simpler; it serializes all bookings for one show, which is fine at a few requests per second per show and worth saying as the simpler alternative.

    In production

    With a database, the same rules become: UPDATE show_seat SET status = 'HELD', hold_id = ?, expires_at = ? WHERE show_id = ? AND seat_id IN (...) AND (status = 'AVAILABLE' OR (status = 'HELD' AND expires_at < now())) inside a transaction, and commit only if the updated row count equals the number of seats. Confirmation is another conditional update WHERE hold_id = ? AND expires_at > now(). The HLD handbook's ticket booking case covers the spike (waiting rooms, caching the seat map).

    P9.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Payment succeeds but confirmation fails

      The hold expired by one second and someone else took a seat. The user has paid.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Confirmation fails and the payment is refunded automatically (a compensation). Better: authorize the payment first, confirm the seats, then capture; a failed confirmation only voids the authorization, so the user is never charged. Use the hold ID as the payment idempotency key so retries never charge twice.

    2. 2
      Do not leave single empty seats

      The theatre does not want isolated single seats left between bookings.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A SeatSelectionRule checked during hold: for each row, simulate the hold and reject it if it leaves a lone available seat between two unavailable ones (or at the aisle). Rules are a chain of validators, so more can be added (no wheelchair seats unless requested).

    3. 3
      Dynamic pricing

      Prices rise as the show fills up, and weekends cost more.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A PricingStrategy that receives the show, the seat category, and the occupancy, chosen per show or per city. Price is computed at hold time and stored in the Hold, so the user pays what they saw even if the price changes before confirmation.

    4. 4
      Cancel a booking

      Users can cancel up to 2 hours before the show for a partial refund.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Add a BOOKED to AVAILABLE transition with the guard "now is more than 2 hours before start", a RefundPolicy strategy for the amount, and a booking status (CONFIRMED, CANCELLED). Released seats become available to holds again.

    Minutes Do

    10-25 Enums, Seat, Movie, Show, ShowSeat with lazy expiry
    25-50 BookingService.hold with sorted locking and all-or-nothing; tests for conflicts
    50-65 confirm and cancelHold; expired-hold test with an injected time
    65-80 Search (shows by movie and city) if required; driver commands

    P9.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: ShowSeat separate from Seat; holds with expiry; all-or-nothing multi-seat holds; no double booking under concurrency; confirm re-checks the hold.
    • Above the bar: ordered locking explained with the deadlock it prevents; lazy expiry; authorize-then-capture payment; the conditional-update database version; pricing captured at hold time.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why sort the seat IDs before locking?
      Reveal

      So every thread acquires locks in the same global order. Two users holding overlapping seats in different orders could otherwise each hold one lock and wait for the other's, a deadlock.

    2. Why is a sweeper thread not required for correctness?
      Reveal

      Every read treats an expired hold as free (lazy expiry). A sweeper only tidies the seat map for display; correctness never depends on it running on time.

    3. Where does the price live, and why there?
      Reveal

      Prices per category belong to the show (same seat, different show, different price). The amount is captured in the hold so later price changes do not affect a user mid-checkout.

    4. How do you prevent one user from holding 200 seats and blocking a show?
      Reveal

      A per-booking seat limit, a per-user limit on active holds, and rate limiting on hold requests.

    Problem 10: Digital wallet

    The fintech problem, and the one closest to payments work: wallets that never go negative, transfers that move money exactly once even when clients retry, locks that cannot deadlock when transfers cross, an append-only ledger that explains every balance, and notifications that never undo a transfer.

    Uses: M9 deadlock and lock ordering, M7 observer, M1 encapsulation

    Try it first60 minutes

    Design a digital wallet: users top up from a bank, transfer to other users, see their balance and statement. Clients retry on timeouts. Many transfers run at once, including A to B while B pays A. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Wallet that guards its balance; transfer(idempotencyKey, from, to, amount) that returns the stored result for a repeated key and moves money once; locks on both wallets taken in a global order; every rule on both sides (funds, the receiver's limit) checked under the locks before either balance changes; a double-entry ledger with a debit and a credit row per transfer; failed transfers recorded as results, not exceptions; listeners called after the money moves and isolated from it; and a conservation check (total money equals total top-ups).

    P10.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Operations? Open wallet, top up from outside, transfer between wallets, balance, statement
    Money? Paise as long; no overdraft; per-transfer limit of 1 lakh rupees; a wallet holds at most 2 lakh (the cap on full-KYC wallets in India)
    Retries? Clients retry on timeout with the same idempotency key; the bank may repeat a top-up callback
    Concurrency? Many transfers at once, in both directions between the same wallets
    Notifications? Notify the receiver after a transfer; a notification failure must not affect the transfer
    Out of scope KYC, currency conversion, refunds to bank (likely follow-ups)

    Invariants: no balance is ever negative or above the cap; each idempotency key moves money at most once; each top-up reference is credited at most once; every transfer writes one debit and one credit of the same amount; the sum of all balances equals the sum of all top-ups.

    P10.2Entities and responsibilities

    Class Responsibility
    Wallet Balance and its lock; canDebit and canCredit answer the rules; debit and credit refuse to break them
    LedgerEntry (record) One signed movement with the balance after it; never changed
    Transaction (record) The result of a transfer request: completed or failed with a reason
    TransactionListener Reacts to completed transfers (notifications, fraud scoring)
    WalletService Idempotency for transfers and top-ups, ordered locking, ledger writes, listener calls

    P10.3Class diagram

    P10.4Key flows

    The ledger after the scenario below, in double-entry form:

    Transaction Wallet Amount Balance after
    upi-topup-1 W1 (Asha) +1,000 1,000
    T1 W1 (Asha) -250 750
    T1 W2 (Ravi) +250 250

    Every internal transfer sums to zero; only top-ups (and later, withdrawals) change the total. A balance can always be rebuilt by summing a wallet's entries, which is how money bugs are found.

    P10.5Code

    Wallet.java
    class Wallet {
    static final long MAX_BALANCE = 20_000_000;  // 2 lakh rupees: the cap on a full-KYC wallet in India
    final String id;
    final String ownerId;
    final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private long balancePaise;                   // guarded by lock

    Wallet(String id, String ownerId) { this.id = id; this.ownerId = ownerId; }

    boolean canDebit(long amount) { return amount > 0 && amount <= balancePaise; }
    boolean canCredit(long amount) { return amount > 0 && amount <= MAX_BALANCE - balancePaise; }

    void debit(long amount) {
        if (!canDebit(amount)) throw new IllegalStateException("debit of " + amount + " not allowed on " + id);
        balancePaise -= amount;
    }

    void credit(long amount) {
        if (!canCredit(amount)) throw new IllegalStateException("credit of " + amount + " not allowed on " + id);
        balancePaise += amount;
    }

    long balance() { return balancePaise; }
}
    WalletService.java: idempotency, ordered locks, ledger, listeners
    class WalletService {
    private static final long MAX_TRANSFER = 10_000_000;                    // 1 lakh rupees
    private final Map<String, Wallet> wallets = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, CompletableFuture<Transaction>> byKey = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final List<LedgerEntry> ledger = Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>());
    private final List<TransactionListener> listeners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    private final Set<String> seenTopUps = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
    private final AtomicLong walletSeq = new AtomicLong(1), txnSeq = new AtomicLong(1);
    private final Clock clock;

    WalletService(Clock clock) { this.clock = clock; }

    Wallet open(String ownerId) {
        Wallet w = new Wallet("W" + walletSeq.getAndIncrement(), ownerId);
        wallets.put(w.id, w);
        return w;
    }

    void subscribe(TransactionListener l) { listeners.add(l); }

    /**
     * Moves money between wallets exactly once per idempotency key.
     * A retry with the same key returns the first result instead of moving money again.
     */
    Transaction transfer(String key, String fromId, String toId, long amount) {
        CompletableFuture<Transaction> mine = new CompletableFuture<>();
        CompletableFuture<Transaction> first = byKey.putIfAbsent(key, mine);
        if (first != null) {                                               // a retry, or a concurrent duplicate
            Transaction t = first.join();                                  // waits if the first is still running
            if (!t.sameRequest(fromId, toId, amount)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("idempotency key reused for a different transfer");
            return t;
        }
        try {
            Transaction t = execute(key, fromId, toId, amount);
            mine.complete(t);
            if (t.status() == TxnStatus.COMPLETED) notifyListeners(t);
            return t;
        } catch (RuntimeException unexpected) {                            // not a business failure: let the client retry
            byKey.remove(key, mine);
            mine.completeExceptionally(unexpected);
            throw unexpected;
        }
    }

    private Transaction execute(String key, String fromId, String toId, long amount) {
        String txnId = "T" + txnSeq.getAndIncrement();
        if (amount <= 0 || amount > MAX_TRANSFER) return failed(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, "amount out of range");
        if (fromId.equals(toId)) return failed(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, "same wallet");
        Wallet from = wallets.get(fromId), to = wallets.get(toId);
        if (from == null || to == null) return failed(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, "unknown wallet");

        Wallet first = from.id.compareTo(to.id) < 0 ? from : to;              // global lock order: no deadlock
        Wallet second = first == from ? to : from;
        first.lock.lock();
        second.lock.lock();
        try {
            // check every rule on both sides before changing either: nothing can fail halfway
            if (!from.canDebit(amount)) return failed(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, "insufficient funds in " + fromId);
            if (!to.canCredit(amount)) return failed(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, "wallet limit reached for " + toId);
            from.debit(amount);
            to.credit(amount);
            synchronized (ledger) {                                        // both rows appear together
                ledger.add(new LedgerEntry(txnId, from.id, -amount, from.balance(), clock.instant()));
                ledger.add(new LedgerEntry(txnId, to.id, amount, to.balance(), clock.instant()));
            }
        } finally {
            second.lock.unlock();
            first.lock.unlock();
        }
        return new Transaction(txnId, key, fromId, toId, amount, TxnStatus.COMPLETED, null);
    }

    /** Money enters from outside (a bank or card top-up). The bank's reference makes a retried top-up a no-op. */
    boolean topUp(String walletId, long amount, String externalRef) {
        Wallet w = wallet(walletId);
        if (!seenTopUps.add(externalRef)) return false;                    // already credited
        w.lock.lock();
        try {
            if (!w.canCredit(amount)) {
                seenTopUps.remove(externalRef);                            // rejected: the bank may retry or refund
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("top-up of " + amount + " not allowed on " + walletId);
            }
            w.credit(amount);
            ledger.add(new LedgerEntry(externalRef, w.id, amount, w.balance(), clock.instant()));
            return true;
        } finally {
            w.lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    long balance(String walletId) {
        Wallet w = wallet(walletId);
        w.lock.lock();
        try { return w.balance(); } finally { w.lock.unlock(); }
    }

    List<LedgerEntry> statement(String walletId) {
        synchronized (ledger) {
            return ledger.stream().filter(e -> e.walletId().equals(walletId)).toList();
        }
    }

    private Wallet wallet(String id) {
        Wallet w = wallets.get(id);
        if (w == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("unknown wallet " + id);
        return w;
    }

    private Transaction failed(String id, String key, String from, String to, long amt, String why) {
        return new Transaction(id, key, from, to, amt, TxnStatus.FAILED, why);
    }

    private void notifyListeners(Transaction t) {                        // after the money moved, outside the locks
        for (TransactionListener l : listeners) {
            try { l.onCompleted(t); } catch (RuntimeException ignored) { /* a failing listener never undoes a transfer */ }
        }
    }
}

    LedgerEntry.java
    import java.time.Instant;

/** Immutable, append-only. Every transfer writes exactly one debit and one credit with the same transaction id. */
record LedgerEntry(String txnId, String walletId, long amountPaise, long balanceAfter, Instant at) {}

    record Transaction(String id, String idempotencyKey, String from, String to, long amountPaise, TxnStatus status, String reason) {

    Demo.java (complete)
    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        WalletService svc = new WalletService(Clock.fixed(Instant.parse("2026-10-21T09:30:00Z"), ZoneOffset.UTC));
        List<String> notified = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
        svc.subscribe(t -> notified.add("notify " + t.to() + ": received " + t.amountPaise() / 100));

        Wallet asha = svc.open("asha"), ravi = svc.open("ravi");
        svc.topUp(asha.id, 100_000, "upi-topup-1");                          // 1,000 rupees
        boolean again = svc.topUp(asha.id, 100_000, "upi-topup-1");          // the bank retries its callback
        Transaction t1 = svc.transfer("req-1", asha.id, ravi.id, 25_000);
        Transaction retry = svc.transfer("req-1", asha.id, ravi.id, 25_000);   // network retry: same key
        Transaction t2 = svc.transfer("req-2", ravi.id, asha.id, 90_000);      // more than ravi has
        System.out.println(t1.id() + " " + t1.status() + "; retry returned " + retry.id() + " (no second debit)");
        System.out.println(t2.id() + " " + t2.status() + ": " + t2.reason());
        System.out.println("retried top-up credited again: " + again);
        System.out.println("balances: asha " + svc.balance(asha.id) / 100 + ", ravi " + svc.balance(ravi.id) / 100);
        System.out.println(notified);
        svc.statement(asha.id).forEach(e -> System.out.println("  " + e.txnId() + " " + e.amountPaise() / 100 + " -> " + e.balanceAfter() / 100));
        check(!again && retry == t1 && svc.balance(asha.id) == 75_000 && svc.balance(ravi.id) == 25_000, "idempotent transfer");

        // 10 wallets, 16 threads, 20,000 random transfers in both directions: money is conserved, no deadlock
        List<Wallet> ws = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) { Wallet w = svc.open("u" + i); svc.topUp(w.id, 1_000_000, "seed-" + i); ws.add(w); }
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16);
        for (int t = 0; t < 16; t++) {
            int tid = t;
            pool.submit(() -> {
                ThreadLocalRandom r = ThreadLocalRandom.current();
                for (int i = 0; i < 1_250; i++) {
                    Wallet a = ws.get(r.nextInt(10)), b = ws.get(r.nextInt(10));
                    if (a != b) svc.transfer("k-" + tid + "-" + i, a.id, b.id, 1 + r.nextInt(50_000));
                }
            });
        }
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "no deadlock");
        long total = 0;
        for (Wallet w : ws) { long b = svc.balance(w.id); check(b >= 0, "negative balance"); total += b; }
        System.out.println("after 20,000 concurrent transfers: total " + total / 100 + " rupees (started with 100000)");
        check(total == 10_000_000, "money conserved");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P10.6Concurrency and correctness

    Risk Defense
    A retry moves money twice putIfAbsent(key, future): the first request claims the key; duplicates wait for and return its result
    Concurrent duplicates with the same key The same map: the second caller blocks on the first caller's future instead of executing
    Key reused for a different transfer Compare the stored request; reject a mismatch
    A to B and B to A deadlock Lock both wallets in wallet-ID order
    Half a transfer Check funds and the receiver's limit under both locks first; then debit and credit cannot fail between them
    A repeated top-up callback The bank's reference is recorded; a second callback with the same reference is a no-op
    A failing notification Listeners run after the locks are released, each in its own try/catch
    A crash during processing In memory, the process is gone. With a database, the debit, the credit, both ledger rows, and the idempotency record commit in one transaction
    Watch out

    Business failures (insufficient funds) are stored as results, so a retry returns the same failure. Unexpected failures (a bug, a timeout from a dependency) remove the key, so the client can retry. Mixing these up either double-charges or blocks a customer forever.

    In production

    This is the shape of real payment ledgers: append-only entries, balances derived or cached from them, idempotency keys stored with request fingerprints and results (Stripe's API keeps keys for 24 hours), and reconciliation jobs that compare the ledger against bank statements. In a database, the ordered locking becomes SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on both wallet rows in ID order, or a single conditional update per wallet.

    P10.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Daily transfer limits

      Each user may send at most 50,000 rupees per day.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A limit check inside the locked section (so two concurrent transfers cannot both pass), using a per-wallet daily counter keyed by date. Put limit rules in a chain of validators (Module 6): KYC level, per-transfer max, daily max, velocity.

    2. 2
      Withdraw to a bank account

      Money leaves the system through an external payout that can fail or time out.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A two-step saga: debit the wallet into a "pending payout" state (a ledger entry against a payout clearing account), call the bank with an idempotency key, then mark the payout completed or reverse the debit on failure. Uncertain outcomes (timeouts) stay pending until a status check or reconciliation resolves them.

    3. 3
      Statements for a month

      Users ask for statements with opening and closing balances.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Query ledger entries by wallet and time range (indexed by wallet and time in a database). Opening balance = the balanceAfter of the last entry before the range, or the sum of all earlier entries. Store monthly snapshots so old statements do not scan all history.

    4. 4
      Detect a ledger bug

      How would you know if balances drifted from the ledger?

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A reconciliation job: for each wallet, sum ledger entries and compare with the stored balance; for each transaction, check that its entries sum to zero; globally, check that total balances equal total top-ups minus withdrawals. Alert on any mismatch.

    P10.8Machine coding plan

    Minutes Do
    0-10 Clarify money units, limits, retries, concurrency; write the four invariants
    10-25 Wallet, LedgerEntry, Transaction, exceptions
    25-50 transfer with ordered locks and the ledger; top-up; balance and statement
    50-65 Idempotency map with the future-based single flight
    65-80 Listeners after commit; demo of retry and failure
    80-90 Concurrency test with conservation check; walk through the database version

    P10.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: no negative balances; ordered locking with the deadlock explained; idempotency keys; a ledger with both sides of each transfer; failed transfers as results.
    • Above the bar: concurrent duplicates handled (not just sequential retries); business vs unexpected failures distinguished; listeners after commit; reconciliation and conservation checks; the database and saga versions.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why check both wallets before changing either?
      Reveal

      Either side can refuse: the sender may be short, the receiver may be at the wallet limit. If the debit ran and then the credit failed, money would vanish or need compensation. Checking every rule under both locks first means the two writes cannot fail halfway.

    2. Why store the whole request with the idempotency key?
      Reveal

      To detect a client bug that reuses a key for a different transfer. Returning the old result for a different request would silently lose the new transfer.

    3. Could you use optimistic locking instead of wallet locks?
      Reveal

      Yes: a version per wallet, and a transaction that updates both wallets only if both versions are unchanged, retrying on conflict. It suits low contention; a hot merchant wallet would retry a lot, where pessimistic locks are steadier.

    4. Why are listeners called outside the locks?
      Reveal

      They may be slow or fail. Holding wallet locks while notifying would block other transfers, and a failing listener must not undo money that already moved.

    Problem 11: In-memory pub-sub message queue

    A small Kafka in one process. The design turns on three ideas: a partition is an append-only log where an offset is just a position; a consumer group shares partitions so each message is processed once per group; and committing after processing gives at-least-once delivery, so handlers must tolerate repeats.

    Uses: M9 locks and granularity, M9 producer-consumer, M7 observer

    Try it first60 minutes

    Design an in-memory message queue: producers publish to topics; several independent services each consume every message; one service can run several consumer threads to share the load; per-user ordering must hold; a crashed consumer must not lose messages. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Topic split into Partitions, each an append-only list with a read-write lock; the key's hash chooses the partition, which preserves per-key order; ConsumerGroup with one committed offset per partition and an assignment of partitions to members, recomputed on join and leave; poll reads from the committed offset, commit moves it forward after processing (at-least-once); worker threads that poll, process, and commit; lag per partition; and a clear answer to "what if a consumer crashes mid-batch".

    P11.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Publish? publish(topic, key, value); the key is optional
    Who receives a message? Every consumer group receives every message; within a group, exactly one member processes it
    Ordering? Messages with the same key are consumed in publish order
    Delivery guarantee? At-least-once: nothing is lost; a crash may cause a repeat
    Push or pull? Pull: consumers poll at their own pace, so a slow consumer never slows the producer
    Replay? A group can move its offset back and reprocess
    Out of scope Retention and deletion, persistence, replication (say how they would fit)

    Invariants: offsets in a partition are dense and never change; each partition has at most one owner in a group at a time; a group's committed offset per partition only moves forward, except by an explicit seek.

    P11.2Entities and responsibilities

    Class Responsibility
    Message (record) Topic, partition, offset, key, value
    Partition Append-only log; append returns the offset; read(from, max) returns a copy
    Topic Owns partitions; chooses one per message (hash of key, or round-robin)
    ConsumerGroup Members, the partition assignment, committed offsets; poll, commit, seek, lag
    ConsumerWorker One thread per member: poll, process, commit, repeat
    Broker Creates topics, routes publishes, creates groups

    P11.3Class diagram

    P11.4How it works

    Three ideas carry the whole design:

    1. The log is the queue. Consuming does not remove anything. A consumer is only a position in the log, so many groups can read the same data at different speeds, and replay is moving a number back.
    2. Partitions give order and parallelism. Order is guaranteed only inside one partition. Hashing the key sends every message for one user to the same partition, so that user's events stay in order, while different users spread across partitions that different members process in parallel.
    3. A group shares partitions, not messages. Each partition has one owner in the group, so a group can have at most as many busy members as partitions. Extra members sit idle; that is why the partition count is a capacity decision.
    Commit when Guarantee Failure mode
    Before processing At-most-once A crash after the commit loses the message
    After processing At-least-once A crash before the commit repeats the message
    In the same transaction as the result Effectively exactly-once Needs the output and the offset in one store
    Key idea

    At-least-once plus idempotent handlers is the practical answer. Make the handler safe to repeat: dedupe by message ID, use upserts, or check the state before acting (the wallet's idempotency keys from Problem 10 are exactly this).

    P11.5Code

    Partition.java: append-only log with a read-write lock
    /** Append-only log. Offsets are positions; messages are never changed or removed (no retention here). */
class Partition {
    private final String topic;
    private final int id;
    private final List<Message> log = new ArrayList<>();
    private final ReentrantReadWriteLock rw = new ReentrantReadWriteLock();   // many readers, one appender

    Partition(String topic, int id) { this.topic = topic; this.id = id; }

    long append(String key, String value) {
        rw.writeLock().lock();
        try {
            long offset = log.size();
            log.add(new Message(topic, id, offset, key, value));
            return offset;
        } finally {
            rw.writeLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    List<Message> read(long fromOffset, int max) {
        rw.readLock().lock();
        try {
            int from = (int) Math.min(fromOffset, log.size());
            int to = Math.min(log.size(), from + max);
            return new ArrayList<>(log.subList(from, to));         // a copy: safe after the lock is released
        } finally {
            rw.readLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    long endOffset() {
        rw.readLock().lock();
        try { return log.size(); } finally { rw.readLock().unlock(); }
    }

    int id() { return id; }
}
    Topic.java: the key picks the partition
    class Topic {
    final String name;
    final List<Partition> partitions = new ArrayList<>();
    private final AtomicInteger roundRobin = new AtomicInteger();

    Topic(String name, int partitionCount) {
        this.name = name;
        for (int i = 0; i < partitionCount; i++) partitions.add(new Partition(name, i));
    }

    /** Same key, same partition: per-key order is preserved. No key: spread evenly. */
    long publish(String key, String value) {
        int p = key == null
                ? Math.floorMod(roundRobin.getAndIncrement(), partitions.size())
                : Math.floorMod(key.hashCode(), partitions.size());
        return partitions.get(p).append(key, value);
    }
}
    ConsumerGroup.java: assignment, offsets, poll, commit, lag
    /** Members share the topic's partitions: each partition has one owner, so per-partition order holds. */
class ConsumerGroup {
    final String name;
    private final Topic topic;
    private final Map<Integer, AtomicLong> committed = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();   // partition -> next offset to read
    private final List<String> members = new ArrayList<>();
    private Map<String, List<Integer>> assignment = Map.of();

    ConsumerGroup(String name, Topic topic) {
        this.name = name;
        this.topic = topic;
        for (Partition p : topic.partitions) committed.put(p.id(), new AtomicLong(0));
    }

    synchronized void join(String consumerId) {
        if (members.contains(consumerId)) return;                // joining twice must not double its share
        members.add(consumerId);
        rebalance();
    }
    synchronized void leave(String consumerId) { members.remove(consumerId); rebalance(); }

    /** Round-robin assignment of partitions to members, recomputed on every membership change. */
    private void rebalance() {
        Map<String, List<Integer>> next = new LinkedHashMap<>();
        for (String m : members) next.put(m, new ArrayList<>());
        for (int p = 0; p < topic.partitions.size() && !members.isEmpty(); p++)
            next.get(members.get(p % members.size())).add(p);
        assignment = next;
    }

    synchronized List<Integer> partitionsOf(String consumerId) {
        return List.copyOf(assignment.getOrDefault(consumerId, List.of()));
    }

    /** Messages after the committed offset on this member's partitions. Nothing is marked read until commit. */
    List<Message> poll(String consumerId, int maxPerPartition) {
        List<Message> out = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int p : partitionsOf(consumerId))
            out.addAll(topic.partitions.get(p).read(committed.get(p).get(), maxPerPartition));
        return out;
    }

    /** Commit after processing: at-least-once delivery. Only moves forward. */
    void commit(String consumerId, Message m) {
        if (!partitionsOf(consumerId).contains(m.partition()))
            throw new IllegalStateException(consumerId + " no longer owns partition " + m.partition());
        committed.get(m.partition()).accumulateAndGet(m.offset() + 1, Math::max);
    }

    /** Replay or skip: move this group's position on one partition. */
    void seek(int partition, long offset) { committed.get(partition).set(offset); }

    Map<Integer, Long> lag() {
        Map<Integer, Long> lag = new HashMap<>();
        for (Partition p : topic.partitions) lag.put(p.id(), p.endOffset() - committed.get(p.id()).get());
        return lag;
    }
}
    ConsumerWorker.java: the worker thread loop
    /** One thread per group member: poll, process, commit, repeat. Membership is managed by the caller. */
class ConsumerWorker implements Runnable {
    private final ConsumerGroup group;
    private final String memberId;
    private final Consumer<Message> handler;
    private volatile boolean running = true;               // written by another thread in stop()

    ConsumerWorker(ConsumerGroup group, String memberId, Consumer<Message> handler) {
        this.group = group;
        this.memberId = memberId;
        this.handler = handler;
    }

    void stop() { running = false; }

    @Override
    public void run() {
        while (running) {
            List<Message> batch = group.poll(memberId, 50);
            if (batch.isEmpty()) { pause(); continue; }     // a real broker long-polls instead of sleeping
            try {
                for (Message m : batch) {
                    handler.accept(m);                      // must be idempotent: it may see m again
                    group.commit(memberId, m);
                }
            } catch (IllegalStateException revoked) {
                // partition moved to another member during a rebalance: drop the rest, poll again
            }
        }
    }

    private static void pause() {
        try { Thread.sleep(2); } catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); }
    }
}

    Broker.java
    import java.util.Map;
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;

class Broker {
    private final Map<String, Topic> topics = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, ConsumerGroup> groups = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();

    Topic createTopic(String name, int partitions) {
        Topic t = new Topic(name, partitions);
        if (topics.putIfAbsent(name, t) != null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("topic exists: " + name);
        return t;
    }

    long publish(String topic, String key, String value) { return topic(topic).publish(key, value); }

    ConsumerGroup group(String groupName, String topicName) {
        return groups.computeIfAbsent(groupName + "@" + topicName, k -> new ConsumerGroup(groupName, topic(topicName)));
    }

    private Topic topic(String name) {
        Topic t = topics.get(name);
        if (t == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no topic " + name);
        return t;
    }
}

    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        Broker broker = new Broker();
        broker.createTopic("orders", 3);
        for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++)
            for (String user : List.of("asha", "ravi", "meera")) broker.publish("orders", user, user + "-order-" + i);

        ConsumerGroup billing = broker.group("billing", "orders");
        billing.join("c1");
        billing.join("c2");
        System.out.println("billing: c1 owns " + billing.partitionsOf("c1") + ", c2 owns " + billing.partitionsOf("c2"));

        List<Message> got = billing.poll("c1", 10);
        System.out.println("c1 got " + got.stream().map(Message::value).toList());
        billing.commit("c1", got.get(0));                  // c1 processed only the first message, then crashed
        billing.leave("c1");                               // rebalance: c2 now owns every partition
        List<Message> redelivered = billing.poll("c2", 10);
        System.out.println("after c1 left, c2 sees " + redelivered.size() + " messages (uncommitted ones come back)");

        ConsumerGroup analytics = broker.group("analytics", "orders");   // an independent group reads everything
        analytics.join("a1");
        List<Message> all = analytics.poll("a1", 10);
        all.forEach(m -> analytics.commit("a1", m));
        analytics.seek(0, 0);                              // replay partition 0 from the start
        System.out.println("analytics read " + all.size() + "; after seek(P0, 0) it sees " + analytics.poll("a1", 10).size() + " again");
        check(redelivered.size() == 8, "at-least-once redelivery");

        broker.createTopic("events", 4);
        ConsumerGroup g = broker.group("workers", "events");
        Set<String> seen = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
        Map<String, Integer> lastSeq = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
        AtomicBoolean orderBroken = new AtomicBoolean();
        List<ConsumerWorker> workers = new ArrayList<>();
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(7);
        for (int c = 0; c < 3; c++) {
            g.join("w" + c);
            ConsumerWorker w = new ConsumerWorker(g, "w" + c, m -> {
                seen.add(m.value());                                     // value = producer:sequence
                String[] ps = m.value().split(":");
                Integer prev = lastSeq.put(ps[0] + "/" + m.key(), Integer.parseInt(ps[1]));
                if (prev != null && prev >= Integer.parseInt(ps[1])) orderBroken.set(true);
            });
            workers.add(w);
            pool.submit(w);
        }
        List<Thread> producers = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int p = 0; p < 4; p++) {
            int pid = p;
            Thread t = new Thread(() -> {
                for (int i = 0; i < 1_000; i++) broker.publish("events", "k" + (i % 20), pid + ":" + i);
            });
            t.start();
            producers.add(t);
        }
        for (Thread t : producers) t.join();
        while (g.lag().values().stream().mapToLong(Long::longValue).sum() > 0) Thread.sleep(5);
        workers.forEach(ConsumerWorker::stop);
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "workers stopped");
        System.out.println("3 workers consumed " + seen.size() + " of 4000; per-key order kept: " + !orderBroken.get() + "; lag " + g.lag());
        check(seen.size() == 4_000 && !orderBroken.get(), "all consumed in order");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    billing: c1 owns [0, 2], c2 owns [1]
c1 got [meera-order-1, meera-order-2, meera-order-3, asha-order-1, ravi-order-1, asha-order-2, ravi-order-2, asha-order-3, ravi-order-3]

    In the demo's orders topic, Meera's orders hash to partition 0 and Asha's and Ravi's to partition 2, so partition 1 is empty and c2 has nothing to do at first: a small picture of why hot keys and partition counts matter.

    P11.6Concurrency

    Shared state Protection Why this choice
    A partition's log ReentrantReadWriteLock Many readers (every group) and one appender at a time; reads return a copy so callers never see the list change
    Round-robin counter AtomicInteger One atomic increment per publish
    Members and assignment synchronized on the group Rare changes; a rebalance must replace the whole assignment at once
    Committed offsets AtomicLong per partition with accumulateAndGet(max) A late commit can never move an offset backwards
    Worker stop flag volatile boolean Written by one thread, read by the worker loop

    A commit from a member that lost the partition in a rebalance is rejected, and the worker drops the rest of its batch. The new owner starts from the last committed offset, so nothing is lost; some messages repeat, which the idempotent handler absorbs.

    Note

    This design uses one number per partition for both "where to read next" and "where to restart after a crash", so a member must commit before it polls again. Kafka keeps two: the in-memory position (advanced by every poll) and the committed offset (advanced by commits). Mention it if asked how to process the next batch while the previous one is still being committed.

    In production

    Kafka, Redpanda, and Pulsar work this way, with the log on disk, replicated across brokers, and deleted by time or size (retention). Kafka fences stale members with a generation number: every rebalance increments it, and commits carrying an old generation are rejected, the same rule as the ownership check here. RabbitMQ and SQS are the other family: messages are removed once acknowledged, with no replay. The HLD handbook covers choosing between them.

    P11.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Push to subscribers instead

      The interviewer wants subscribers to receive messages through a callback, without polling.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Observer (Module 7) with one queue and one delivery thread per subscriber: publish appends to each subscriber's BlockingQueue and returns; each subscriber's thread takes from its queue and calls the callback. A slow subscriber then only delays itself. Bound each queue and decide what happens when it is full: block the publisher, drop the oldest, or disconnect the subscriber.

    2. 2
      Retention

      Memory grows forever.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Split each partition's log into segments (for example every 10,000 messages) and delete whole segments older than the retention time or beyond the size limit. Offsets stay the same; a group whose offset points into a deleted segment is moved to the earliest remaining offset (Kafka calls this the offset reset policy).

    3. 3
      Dead-letter queue

      One message always makes the handler throw, and the partition is stuck.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Retry a few times with backoff, then publish the message to a topic.dlq topic with the error, commit it, and move on. A separate process inspects and replays the dead letters. Without this, one bad message blocks every message behind it in that partition.

    4. 4
      More consumers than partitions

      The team adds 10 workers to a group on a 4-partition topic, and throughput does not change.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Only 4 members can own partitions; the other 6 are idle. Raise the partition count (planned up front, because changing it moves keys to different partitions and breaks per-key order during the change), or process messages from one partition in parallel inside a worker when order does not matter.

    Minutes Do

    15-35 Message, Partition (append, read, lock), Topic (key hashing), Broker
    35-60 ConsumerGroup: join, leave, round-robin assignment, poll, commit
    60-80 ConsumerWorker threads; demo with producers and workers; verify count and per-key order

    P11.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: offsets instead of deleting messages; per-key ordering through partitions; groups with one owner per partition; commit after processing, with the repeat explained; a thread-safe log.
    • Above the bar: rebalance with stale-commit rejection; lag as the health metric; position vs committed offset; idempotent handlers; dead letters; why partitions cap a group's parallelism.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why not delete a message once it is consumed?
      Reveal

      Several groups read the same topic at different speeds, and replay needs old data. An offset per group lets every group keep its own place in a single shared log.

    2. How is order preserved for one user while still processing in parallel?
      Reveal

      Hash the user ID to a partition, so all of that user's messages land in one partition, and give each partition to one member of the group. Different users are spread across partitions processed in parallel.

    3. A consumer crashes after processing a message but before committing. What happens?
      Reveal

      After the rebalance, the new owner reads from the last committed offset and processes that message again. The handler must be idempotent.

    4. What does lag tell you?
      Reveal

      End offset minus committed offset per partition: how far behind a group is. Rising lag means consumers are slower than producers; it is the main alert for a queue.

    Problem 12: Task scheduler

    Build a small ScheduledExecutorService: a priority queue of tasks ordered by run time, one dispatcher thread that sleeps exactly until the next task is due and wakes early when a sooner one arrives, a worker pool that runs tasks, recurring tasks at a fixed rate or with a fixed delay, and cancellation that is safe at any moment.

    Uses: M9 producer-consumer, M9 atomics, M7 state machines
    Your status

    Try it first60 minutes

    Design a task scheduler: run a task once after a delay, or repeatedly every N seconds; cancel a task; run many tasks in parallel; a failing task must not break the scheduler. Show how the scheduler knows when to wake up. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: ScheduledTask with a next run time and a state machine (scheduled, running, done, failed, cancelled); a PriorityQueue ordered by next run time (and a sequence number for ties) under a lock; one dispatcher thread that waits on a Condition with awaitNanos(head - now) and is signalled when a new task becomes the head; a fixed thread pool that runs due tasks; recurring tasks re-queued after each run with fixed-rate or fixed-delay timing; lazy cancellation with an atomic state; task exceptions caught and recorded; and a shutdown that cancels waiting tasks.

    P12.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Kinds of task? Once after a delay; fixed rate (every N by the clock); fixed delay (N after each run ends)
    Precision? Milliseconds; a task never runs before its time and starts promptly after it
    Parallelism? A pool of K worker threads; a slow task must not delay others' start times
    Overlap? A recurring task never runs twice at the same time
    Failures? A throwing task is recorded; a recurring task keeps its schedule
    Cancel? Any time; a running task finishes its current run and is not rescheduled
    Out of scope Persistence across restarts, cron expressions, several machines (deep dives)

    Invariants: no task runs before its due time; each run is claimed by exactly one worker; a cancelled task never starts again; a recurring task has at most one run in flight.

    P12.2Entities and responsibilities

    Class Responsibility
    TaskState (enum) SCHEDULED, RUNNING, DONE, FAILED, CANCELLED
    ScheduledTask The action, kind, period, next run time; state changes by compare-and-set; run count, last error
    TaskScheduler Priority queue, lock and condition, dispatcher thread, worker pool; schedule, cancel, shutdown

    P12.3Class diagram

    P12.4How it works

    The dispatcher's loop is the heart of it, and it is worth saying out loud in the interview:

    1. Look at the head of the queue. Empty: wait until signalled.
    2. Not due yet: wait for exactly due - now, but wake early if signalled. A new task that becomes the head signals, so a task due in 100 ms is not stuck behind one due in 300 ms.
    3. Due: remove it and hand it to the worker pool. Never run it on the dispatcher thread, or one slow task would delay every other start.
    Analogy

    The dispatcher is a hotel night porter with a list of wake-up calls sorted by time. He sets one alarm for the earliest call and sleeps. If a guest asks for an earlier call, the porter resets the alarm. When the alarm rings, he hands the call to a free receptionist and sets the next alarm. He never makes the calls himself, or a long conversation would make him miss the next one.

    P12.5Code

    TaskScheduler.java: queue, dispatcher, workers, shutdown
    class TaskScheduler {
    private final PriorityQueue<ScheduledTask> queue = new PriorityQueue<>(
            Comparator.comparingLong(ScheduledTask::nextRunNanos).thenComparingLong(ScheduledTask::seq));
    private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private final Condition changed = lock.newCondition();   // signalled when a new earliest task arrives
    private final Map<Long, ScheduledTask> tasks = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong();
    private final ExecutorService workers;
    private final Thread dispatcher = new Thread(this::dispatchLoop, "dispatcher");
    private long seq;                  // guarded by lock
    private boolean running = true;    // guarded by lock

    TaskScheduler(int workerThreads) { workers = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(workerThreads); }

    void start() { dispatcher.start(); }                    // separate from the constructor: build first, then run

    long schedule(String name, Runnable r, Duration delay) {
        return submit(name, r, ScheduledTask.Kind.ONCE, delay, Duration.ZERO);
    }
    long scheduleAtFixedRate(String name, Runnable r, Duration initialDelay, Duration period) {
        return submit(name, r, ScheduledTask.Kind.FIXED_RATE, initialDelay, period);
    }
    long scheduleWithFixedDelay(String name, Runnable r, Duration initialDelay, Duration delay) {
        return submit(name, r, ScheduledTask.Kind.FIXED_DELAY, initialDelay, delay);
    }

    boolean cancel(long id) {
        ScheduledTask t = tasks.get(id);
        return t != null && t.cancel();                     // lazy: the dispatcher skips it when it reaches the head
    }

    TaskState state(long id) { return tasks.get(id).state(); }
    int runs(long id) { return tasks.get(id).runs(); }

    private long submit(String name, Runnable r, ScheduledTask.Kind kind, Duration delay, Duration period) {
        if (delay.isNegative()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("negative delay");
        if (kind != ScheduledTask.Kind.ONCE && (period.isZero() || period.isNegative()))
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("period must be positive");
        ScheduledTask t = new ScheduledTask(ids.incrementAndGet(), name, r, kind,
                System.nanoTime() + delay.toNanos(), period.toNanos());
        tasks.put(t.id, t);
        if (!enqueue(t)) throw new IllegalStateException("scheduler is shut down");
        return t.id;
    }

    private boolean enqueue(ScheduledTask t) {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            if (!running) return false;
            t.setSeq(seq++);
            queue.add(t);
            if (queue.peek() == t) changed.signal();         // earlier than what the dispatcher waits for: re-plan
            return true;
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    private void dispatchLoop() {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            while (running) {
                ScheduledTask head = queue.peek();
                if (head == null) { changed.await(); continue; }
                long wait = head.nextRunNanos() - System.nanoTime();
                if (wait > 0) { changed.awaitNanos(wait); continue; }   // re-check: a sooner task may have arrived
                queue.poll();
                if (head.state() == TaskState.CANCELLED) continue;
                workers.execute(() -> runOnce(head));
            }
        } catch (InterruptedException e) {
            Thread.currentThread().interrupt();
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    private void runOnce(ScheduledTask t) {
        if (!t.tryStart()) return;                          // cancelled after it was handed over
        t.runAction();                                      // a failing task cannot kill the worker
        if (t.finishRun(System.nanoTime()) && !enqueue(t)) t.cancel();
    }

    /** Stops accepting tasks, cancels waiting ones, lets running ones finish. */
    void shutdown() throws InterruptedException {
        lock.lock();
        try {
            running = false;
            queue.forEach(ScheduledTask::cancel);
            queue.clear();
            changed.signal();
        } finally {
            lock.unlock();
        }
        dispatcher.join();
        workers.shutdown();
        if (!workers.awaitTermination(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)) workers.shutdownNow();
    }
}
    ScheduledTask.java: timing and the atomic state machine
    final class ScheduledTask {
    enum Kind { ONCE, FIXED_RATE, FIXED_DELAY }

    final long id;
    final String name;
    private final Runnable action;
    private final Kind kind;
    private final long periodNanos;
    private long nextRunNanos;        // changed only while the task is out of the queue
    private long seq;                 // tie-breaker: equal times run in submission order
    private final AtomicReference<TaskState> state = new AtomicReference<>(TaskState.SCHEDULED);
    private final AtomicInteger runs = new AtomicInteger();
    private volatile RuntimeException lastError;

    ScheduledTask(long id, String name, Runnable action, Kind kind, long firstRunNanos, long periodNanos) {
        this.id = id;
        this.name = name;
        this.action = action;
        this.kind = kind;
        this.nextRunNanos = firstRunNanos;
        this.periodNanos = periodNanos;
    }

    /** Claim one run. Fails if the task was cancelled while it waited in the queue. */
    boolean tryStart() {
        if (!state.compareAndSet(TaskState.SCHEDULED, TaskState.RUNNING)) return false;
        runs.incrementAndGet();
        return true;
    }

    void runAction() {
        try {
            action.run();
            lastError = null;
        } catch (RuntimeException e) {
            lastError = e;            // recorded, never thrown into the worker thread
        }
    }

    /** After a run: true if the task should go back into the queue. */
    boolean finishRun(long nowNanos) {
        if (kind == Kind.ONCE) {
            state.compareAndSet(TaskState.RUNNING, lastError == null ? TaskState.DONE : TaskState.FAILED);
            return false;
        }
        nextRunNanos = kind == Kind.FIXED_RATE ? nextRunNanos + periodNanos : nowNanos + periodNanos;
        return state.compareAndSet(TaskState.RUNNING, TaskState.SCHEDULED);   // false if cancelled during the run
    }

    boolean cancel() {
        while (true) {
            TaskState s = state.get();
            if (s == TaskState.DONE || s == TaskState.FAILED || s == TaskState.CANCELLED) return false;
            if (state.compareAndSet(s, TaskState.CANCELLED)) return true;
        }
    }

    long nextRunNanos() { return nextRunNanos; }
    long seq() { return seq; }
    void setSeq(long seq) { this.seq = seq; }
    TaskState state() { return state.get(); }
    int runs() { return runs.get(); }
}
