    Demo.java (complete)
    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        TaskScheduler s = new TaskScheduler(2);
        s.start();
        List<String> log = Collections.synchronizedList(new ArrayList<>());
        s.schedule("report", () -> log.add("report"), ms(300));
        s.schedule("reminder", () -> log.add("reminder"), ms(100));   // sooner than the head: the dispatcher re-plans
        s.schedule("cleanup", () -> log.add("cleanup"), ms(200));
        long broken = s.schedule("broken", () -> { throw new IllegalStateException("db down"); }, ms(50));
        long beat = s.scheduleAtFixedRate("heartbeat", () -> { }, ms(0), ms(40));
        AtomicInteger syncCalls = new AtomicInteger();
        long sync = s.scheduleWithFixedDelay("sync", () -> {
            if (syncCalls.incrementAndGet() == 2) throw new IllegalStateException("timeout");   // fails once
        }, ms(0), ms(60));

        Thread.sleep(400);
        s.cancel(beat);
        s.cancel(sync);
        int beatsAtCancel = s.runs(beat);
        Thread.sleep(150);
        System.out.println("one-shots ran in time order: " + log);
        System.out.println("broken: " + s.state(broken) + "; sync kept running after its failure: " + (s.runs(sync) >= 4));
        System.out.println("heartbeat ran every 40 ms: " + (beatsAtCancel >= 5) + "; state " + s.state(beat)
                + "; runs after cancel: " + (s.runs(beat) - beatsAtCancel));
        long never = s.schedule("never", () -> log.add("never"), ms(10_000));
        s.shutdown();
        System.out.println("after shutdown, the waiting task is " + s.state(never));
        check(log.equals(List.of("reminder", "cleanup", "report")), "order");
        check(s.state(broken) == TaskState.FAILED && s.runs(beat) == beatsAtCancel, "states");

        TaskScheduler s2 = new TaskScheduler(4);
        s2.start();
        int n = 2_000;
        CountDownLatch done = new CountDownLatch(n);
        AtomicIntegerArray ranTimes = new AtomicIntegerArray(n);
        AtomicInteger early = new AtomicInteger();
        List<Thread> submitters = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int k = 0; k < 4; k++) {
            int part = k;
            Thread t = new Thread(() -> {
                for (int i = part; i < n; i += 4) {
                    int task = i;
                    long delay = ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextLong(0, 100);
                    long due = System.nanoTime() + TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS.toNanos(delay);
                    s2.schedule("t" + task, () -> {
                        if (System.nanoTime() < due) early.incrementAndGet();
                        ranTimes.incrementAndGet(task);
                        done.countDown();
                    }, ms(delay));
                }
            });
            t.start();
            submitters.add(t);
        }
        for (Thread t : submitters) t.join();
        check(done.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "all ran");
        s2.shutdown();
        boolean once = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) once &= ranTimes.get(i) == 1;
        System.out.println(n + " tasks from 4 threads: each ran exactly once: " + once + "; ran early: " + early.get());
        check(once && early.get() == 0, "load");
    }

    static Duration ms(long millis) { return Duration.ofMillis(millis); }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P12.6Concurrency

    Shared state Protection Why
    The priority queue ReentrantLock PriorityQueue is not thread-safe; callers, the dispatcher, and workers all touch it
    "A sooner task arrived" Condition signalled when the new task is the head The dispatcher sleeps the exact time but never misses an earlier task
    A task's state AtomicReference with compare-and-set Cancel, start, and finish can race; exactly one transition wins
    A task's next run time Changed only while the task is out of the queue Changing a key inside a PriorityQueue corrupts its order silently
    Equal run times Sequence number as a tie-breaker Tasks due at the same moment run in submission order

    Cancellation is lazy: cancel only flips the state, and the dispatcher discards cancelled tasks when they reach the head. Removing from the middle of a heap is O(n); lazy removal is O(1) and the cost is memory until the task's time comes (the JDK's setRemoveOnCancelPolicy exists for when that memory matters).

    Watch out

    The JDK's ScheduledExecutorService silently stops a periodic task forever after one run throws, with no log line. This is a classic production bug: a nightly job stops running and nobody notices. Wrap periodic task bodies in try/catch, or use a scheduler that, like this one, records the failure and keeps the schedule.

    Note

    The JDK shortcut for the queue and the waiting is DelayQueue: elements implement Delayed, and take() blocks until the head is due. A dispatcher thread that loops on take() and submits to a pool is a complete one-screen scheduler. Write the lock and condition version when the interviewer wants to see the mechanism; mention DelayQueue either way.

    In production

    ScheduledThreadPoolExecutor is built the same way: a heap ordered by time and then sequence number, and periodic tasks re-queued after each run. One difference: it has no separate dispatcher; one idle worker at a time (the "leader") sleeps until the head is due, and the others wait behind it. Spring's @Scheduled runs on it. Jobs that must survive restarts or run on one machine out of many use Quartz with a database job store, ShedLock, or a workflow engine; the HLD handbook covers the distributed version.

    P12.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Cron expressions

      Run at 9:00 every weekday.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A Trigger strategy with nextRunAfter(Instant): one implementation for fixed rate, one for fixed delay, one for cron (parse the expression into allowed minutes, hours, and days, then search forward for the next match). ScheduledTask asks its trigger for the next time instead of adding a period. Use wall-clock time with a time zone for cron, and decide what happens across daylight-saving changes.

    2. 2
      Survive a restart

      Tasks must not be lost if the process dies.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Store tasks in a table (id, next_run_at, kind, payload, status) indexed by next_run_at. The dispatcher queries due rows instead of a heap, and claims each with a conditional update (status = 'RUNNING' WHERE status = 'SCHEDULED'), which also makes several scheduler instances safe. Runs may repeat after a crash, so task bodies must be idempotent.

    3. 3
      Priorities

      Two tasks are due at the same time; one is more important.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Add priority to the comparator after the due time, or give high-priority tasks their own worker pool so a flood of low-priority work cannot starve them. Separate pools are usually the better answer: ordering only helps when tasks are waiting, not when all workers are busy with long tasks.

    4. 4
      Timeouts

      A task hangs forever and holds a worker.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Submit through Future and cancel it after a deadline with future.cancel(true), which interrupts the thread; the task must respond to interruption (blocking calls do; tight loops must check Thread.interrupted()). Record a TIMED_OUT result. Without cooperative code, a hung thread can only be abandoned, so size the pool with that in mind.

    P12.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: priority queue by time; a dispatcher that waits for the head instead of polling; a worker pool separate from the dispatcher; fixed rate vs fixed delay explained; cancellation; task failures contained.
    • Above the bar: wake-up on a new earliest task; atomic state transitions for cancel races; the "never mutate a key inside a heap" rule; tie-breaking by sequence; the JDK periodic-task exception trap; DelayQueue as the shortcut; the persistent, multi-instance version.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why not have the dispatcher check the queue every 10 ms?
      Reveal

      Polling either wastes CPU or adds up to 10 ms of lateness. Waiting exactly until the head is due, and being signalled when a sooner task arrives, gives prompt starts with an idle thread.

    2. Why does the dispatcher not run the task itself?
      Reveal

      A task that takes 5 seconds would delay every task due during those 5 seconds. The dispatcher only decides when; the workers do the running.

    3. How do you stop a recurring task from overlapping with itself?
      Reveal

      Re-queue it only after the current run finishes. The next run time is computed then, so there is never a second copy in the queue while one is running.

    4. What happens if you cancel a task while it is running?
      Reveal

      The state changes from RUNNING to CANCELLED. The current run completes (it is not interrupted), and the attempt to move back to SCHEDULED fails, so it is never re-queued.

    Try it first30 minutes

    Design tic-tac-toe for an N x N board and two or more players, where a line of N marks wins. Support a computer player and undo. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Board that rejects off-board and taken cells; Game that owns the turn, the status (in progress, won, draw), and a move history; Player with a mark and a PlayerStrategy (scripted for tests, a bot, or console input); a WinTracker with per-player counters for each row, column, and the two diagonals, so each move is checked in O(1); undo that pops the last move and reverses every counter; and moves after the end rejected.

    P13.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Board size? N x N, N at least 3; a full row, column, or diagonal of one mark wins
    Players? Two or more, each with a distinct mark, in a fixed order
    Draw? The board fills with no line
    Computer player? Yes, a simple one; humans and bots must be interchangeable
    Undo? Take back the last move, even a winning one
    Out of scope Networking, ranking, time limits (likely follow-ups)

    Invariants: a cell holds at most one mark; only the current player moves; nothing moves after a win or a draw; undo restores the board, the counters, the turn, and the status together.

    WinTracker.java: counters instead of a scan
    /** Counts each player's marks per row, column, and diagonal, so a win is detected in O(1) per move. */
class WinTracker {
    private final int n;
    private final int[][] rows, cols;          // [player][index]
    private final int[] diag, anti;            // [player]

    WinTracker(int n, int players) {
        this.n = n;
        rows = new int[players][n];
        cols = new int[players][n];
        diag = new int[players];
        anti = new int[players];
    }

    /** Records a mark; true if it completes a line. */
    boolean add(int p, int r, int c) {
        rows[p][r]++;
        cols[p][c]++;
        if (r == c) diag[p]++;
        if (r + c == n - 1) anti[p]++;
        return rows[p][r] == n || cols[p][c] == n || diag[p] == n || anti[p] == n;
    }

    void remove(int p, int r, int c) {         // for undo
        rows[p][r]--;
        cols[p][c]--;
        if (r == c) diag[p]--;
        if (r + c == n - 1) anti[p]--;
    }

    /** Would a mark here complete a line? Lets a bot look one move ahead without changing anything. */
    boolean wouldWin(int p, int r, int c) {
        return rows[p][r] + 1 == n || cols[p][c] + 1 == n
                || (r == c && diag[p] + 1 == n) || (r + c == n - 1 && anti[p] + 1 == n);
    }
}
    Game.java: turns, status, history, undo
    class Game {
    private final Board board;
    private final WinTracker tracker;
    private final List<Player> players;
    private final Deque<Move> history = new ArrayDeque<>();
    private int turn = 0;                                        // index of the player to move
    private GameStatus status = GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS;
    private Player winner;

    Game(int n, List<Player> players) {
        if (players.size() < 2) throw new IllegalArgumentException("need at least 2 players");
        if (players.stream().map(Player::mark).distinct().count() != players.size())
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("marks must be distinct");
        this.board = new Board(n);
        this.tracker = new WinTracker(n, players.size());
        this.players = List.copyOf(players);
    }

    /** The current player's strategy picks a cell; the game validates and applies it. */
    GameStatus playTurn() {
        int[] cell = players.get(turn).strategy().chooseCell(this, turn);
        return play(cell[0], cell[1]);
    }

    GameStatus play(int r, int c) {
        if (status != GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS) throw new IllegalStateException("game is over: " + status);
        Player p = players.get(turn);
        board.place(r, c, p.mark());                             // validates bounds and emptiness
        history.push(new Move(turn, r, c));
        if (tracker.add(turn, r, c)) { status = GameStatus.WON; winner = p; }
        else if (board.isFull()) status = GameStatus.DRAW;
        else turn = (turn + 1) % players.size();
        return status;
    }

    /** Takes back the last move, including a winning one. */
    void undo() {
        Move m = history.poll();
        if (m == null) throw new IllegalStateException("nothing to undo");
        board.clear(m.row(), m.col());
        tracker.remove(m.player(), m.row(), m.col());
        status = GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS;
        winner = null;
        turn = m.player();
    }

    GameStatus playToEnd() {
        while (status == GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS) playTurn();
        return status;
    }

    boolean wouldWin(int player, int r, int c) { return tracker.wouldWin(player, r, c); }
    Board board() { return board; }
    int playerCount() { return players.size(); }
    GameStatus status() { return status; }
    Optional<Player> winner() { return Optional.ofNullable(winner); }
}
    Board.java
    class Board {
    static final char EMPTY = '.';
    private final int n;
    private final char[][] cells;
    private int filled;

    Board(int n) {
        if (n < 3) throw new IllegalArgumentException("board must be at least 3 x 3");
        this.n = n;
        this.cells = new char[n][n];
        for (char[] row : cells) java.util.Arrays.fill(row, EMPTY);
    }

    void place(int r, int c, char mark) {
        if (r < 0 || r >= n || c < 0 || c >= n) throw new IllegalArgumentException("cell (" + r + ", " + c + ") is off the board");
        if (cells[r][c] != EMPTY) throw new IllegalArgumentException("cell (" + r + ", " + c + ") is taken");
        cells[r][c] = mark;
        filled++;
    }

    void clear(int r, int c) {
        if (cells[r][c] == EMPTY) throw new IllegalStateException("cell (" + r + ", " + c + ") is already empty");
        cells[r][c] = EMPTY;
        filled--;
    }

    boolean isEmpty(int r, int c) { return cells[r][c] == EMPTY; }
    boolean isFull() { return filled == n * n; }
    char at(int r, int c) { return cells[r][c]; }
    int size() { return n; }
}
    PlayerStrategy.java
    /** Where a player moves next: a human reading input, a scripted test, or a bot. */
interface PlayerStrategy {
    int[] chooseCell(Game game, int me);
}
    SimpleBot.java: win, block, center, first free
    /** Win if possible, else block the next player's win, else center, else the first free cell. */
class SimpleBot implements PlayerStrategy {
    public int[] chooseCell(Game game, int me) {
        int n = game.board().size();
        int next = (me + 1) % game.playerCount();
        for (int target : new int[] {me, next})                       // first my win, then their threat
            for (int r = 0; r < n; r++)
                for (int c = 0; c < n; c++)
                    if (game.board().isEmpty(r, c) && game.wouldWin(target, r, c)) return new int[] {r, c};
        if (game.board().isEmpty(n / 2, n / 2)) return new int[] {n / 2, n / 2};
        for (int r = 0; r < n; r++)
            for (int c = 0; c < n; c++)
                if (game.board().isEmpty(r, c)) return new int[] {r, c};
        throw new IllegalStateException("no free cell");
    }
}

    ScriptedStrategy.java
    import java.util.ArrayDeque;
import java.util.Deque;
import java.util.List;

/** Plays a fixed list of moves: stands in for a human in tests and demos. */
class ScriptedStrategy implements PlayerStrategy {
    private final Deque<int[]> moves;
    ScriptedStrategy(List<int[]> moves) { this.moves = new ArrayDeque<>(moves); }
    public int[] chooseCell(Game game, int me) {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException("script ran out of moves");
        return moves.poll();
    }
}

    /** Console output lives here, not in Board: the model does not know about printing. */
final class BoardRenderer {
    private BoardRenderer() { }

    static String render(Board b) {
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
        for (int r = 0; r < b.size(); r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < b.size(); c++) sb.append(b.at(r, c)).append(c + 1 < b.size() ? " " : "");
            sb.append('\n');
        }
        return sb.toString();
    }
}

    Demo.java (complete)
    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Player asha = new Player("Asha", 'X', new ScriptedStrategy(List.of(
                new int[] {1, 1}, new int[] {0, 0}, new int[] {2, 2})));
        Player ravi = new Player("Ravi", 'O', new ScriptedStrategy(List.of(
                new int[] {0, 1}, new int[] {0, 2})));
        Game game = new Game(3, List.of(asha, ravi));
        GameStatus end = game.playToEnd();                     // X takes the main diagonal on move 5
        System.out.print(BoardRenderer.render(game.board()));
        System.out.println(end + ": " + game.winner().map(Player::name).orElse("nobody"));
        try { game.play(1, 0); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }
        game.undo();                                            // take back the winning move
        System.out.println("after undo: " + game.status() + ", cell (2, 2) empty: " + game.board().isEmpty(2, 2));
        try { game.play(0, 0); } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) { System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }
        check(end == GameStatus.WON && game.status() == GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS, "win and undo");

        Game bots = new Game(3, List.of(new Player("Bot X", 'X', new SimpleBot()), new Player("Bot O", 'O', new SimpleBot())));
        System.out.println("bot vs bot on 3 x 3: " + bots.playToEnd() + " " + bots.winner().map(Player::name).orElse(""));
        Game four = new Game(4, List.of(new Player("A", 'A', new SimpleBot()), new Player("B", 'B', new SimpleBot()),
                new Player("C", 'C', new SimpleBot())));
        System.out.println("three bots on 4 x 4: " + four.playToEnd() + " " + four.winner().map(Player::name).orElse(""));
        System.out.print(BoardRenderer.render(four.board()));
        check(bots.status() != GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS && four.status() != GameStatus.IN_PROGRESS, "games end");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    The simple bot lost to itself: playing "first free cell" let its opponent build a fork (two threats at once). That is the expected limit of a one-move look-ahead; the deep dive below shows the unbeatable version.

    P13.6Hard parts

    The O(1) check. Scanning after every move is O(N^2) per move, which interviewers accept for 3 x 3 but ask you to improve. A mark at (r, c) can only complete row r, column c, and the diagonals through it, so per-player counters for those lines are enough. For two players a common variant keeps one signed counter per line (+1 for X, -1 for O) and wins at +N or -N.

    Undo. The history stores moves, not board copies (the command idea from Module 7). Undo must reverse everything the move changed: the cell, four counters, the turn, and the status. Forgetting the counters makes the game declare wins that no longer exist.

    Strategy for players. The game asks the current player's strategy for a cell and then validates it like any other move. Bots get no special path into the board, so a buggy bot cannot cheat, and tests replace humans with scripts.

    Concurrency. None in the local game. An online version runs each game on one thread at a time (a per-game lock or a single-threaded actor), and rejects a move whose player is not the one to move, which also handles a double click arriving twice.

    P13.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      K in a row on a large board

      Gomoku: a 15 x 15 board where 5 in a row wins.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Counters per whole row no longer work, because a row can hold five marks without five in a row. After a move, walk from the placed cell in each of four directions (horizontal, vertical, two diagonals), counting consecutive marks both ways. That is O(K) per move, still independent of the board size.

    2. 2
      An unbeatable bot

      The simple bot loses to forks.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Minimax: try every legal move, recurse with the other player, score wins +1, losses -1, draws 0, and pick the best guaranteed outcome. 3 x 3 has under 6,000 reachable positions, so it runs instantly; alpha-beta pruning and a memo of seen positions make larger boards feasible. It is just another PlayerStrategy.

    3. 3
      Chess from this skeleton

      What stays and what changes?

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Game, Player, turns, history, undo, and the status machine stay. The board holds pieces; each piece type has a move-generation strategy (polymorphism); validation adds "does not leave your own king in check"; the status gains CHECKMATE and STALEMATE; moves become richer commands (captures, castling, promotion) that know how to undo themselves.

    4. 4
      Replay a game for a spectator

      How would you support watching a finished game move by move?

      Write your answer, then reveal

      The move history already is the game record. Store it, then rebuild a fresh Game by replaying the moves through play, which re-validates each one. This is event sourcing in miniature.

    Minutes Do

    P13.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: validated moves; turn and status owned by the game; O(1) win check explained; draw detection; strategies for players; undo that reverses everything.
    • Above the bar: N players and N x N without special cases; K-in-a-row variant; minimax as a strategy; the skeleton mapped to chess; replay from the move history.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why does the win check only look at four lines?
      Reveal

      A new mark can only complete lines that pass through its cell: its row, its column, and the main or anti-diagonal if it lies on them. Every other line was already checked by earlier moves.

    2. Why is Board not responsible for detecting a win?
      Reveal

      The board knows cells; winning is a rule of the game, and rules vary (K in a row, misere variants). Keeping the rule in the tracker and the game lets the board stay simple and reusable.

    3. What must undo restore?
      Reveal

      The cell, the counters for its row, column, and diagonals, the player to move, and the status (a winning move undone means the game is in progress again).

    4. How do you test a bot?
      Reveal

      Set up a board where the bot must win in one move, and one where it must block; assert the chosen cell. Scripted strategies drive the other player.

    Problem 14: Meeting room scheduler

    Calendar and room booking is an interval problem dressed as a design problem. The data structure is a sorted map per room where only two neighbors can clash; the design is a selection strategy that keeps big rooms for big meetings; the correctness is a per-room lock so two people never get the same slot, and all-or-nothing booking for recurring series.

    Try it first45 minutes

    Design a meeting room scheduler: rooms with capacities, book a room for a time range (any suitable room, or a specific one), weekly recurring meetings, cancellation, and a query for free rooms. Many people book at once. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Interval as a half-open [start, end) value object with overlaps; RoomCalendar per room with a TreeMap from start to booking, checked with floorEntry and ceilingEntry in O(log n); a RoomSelectionStrategy (smallest room that fits); SchedulerService that tries candidates in order and books each atomically under that room's lock; recurring meetings checked completely, then inserted, under the same lock; cancellation; and a clear note that "free rooms" is a snapshot that a later booking may still lose.

    Interval.java: half-open ranges
    /** Half-open [start, end): a meeting ending at 11:00 does not clash with one starting at 11:00. */
record Interval(LocalDateTime start, LocalDateTime end) {
    Interval {
        if (!start.isBefore(end)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("start must be before end");
    }

    boolean overlaps(Interval o) { return start.isBefore(o.end) && o.start.isBefore(end); }

    Interval plus(Duration d) { return new Interval(start.plus(d), end.plus(d)); }
}
    RoomCalendar.java: TreeMap per room
    /** One room's bookings, sorted by start. Callers hold `lock` while checking and changing. */
class RoomCalendar {
    final Room room;
    final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
    private final TreeMap<java.time.LocalDateTime, Booking> byStart = new TreeMap<>();

    RoomCalendar(Room room) { this.room = room; }

    /** O(log n): only the booking starting just before and the one starting just after can overlap. */
    boolean isFree(Interval i) {
        Map.Entry<java.time.LocalDateTime, Booking> before = byStart.floorEntry(i.start());
        if (before != null && before.getValue().interval().overlaps(i)) return false;
        Map.Entry<java.time.LocalDateTime, Booking> after = byStart.ceilingEntry(i.start());
        return after == null || !after.getValue().interval().overlaps(i);
    }

    void add(Booking b) {
        if (!isFree(b.interval())) throw new IllegalStateException("overlap in " + room.id());   // a caller bug
        byStart.put(b.interval().start(), b);
    }

    void remove(Booking b) { byStart.remove(b.interval().start(), b); }

    List<Booking> all() { return new ArrayList<>(byStart.values()); }
}
    SchedulerService.java: candidates, per-room locks, series
    class SchedulerService {
    private final Map<String, RoomCalendar> calendars = new LinkedHashMap<>();   // fixed after construction
    private final Map<String, Booking> bookings = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final RoomSelectionStrategy selection;
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong(1), seriesIds = new AtomicLong(1);

    SchedulerService(List<Room> rooms, RoomSelectionStrategy selection) {
        rooms.forEach(r -> calendars.put(r.id(), new RoomCalendar(r)));
        this.selection = selection;
    }

    /** Any suitable room: try candidates in strategy order; each try is atomic for that room. */
    Booking book(String organizer, String title, int attendees, Interval when) {
        List<Room> rooms = calendars.values().stream().map(c -> c.room).toList();
        for (Room r : selection.candidates(rooms, attendees)) {
            Optional<Booking> b = tryBook(r.id(), organizer, title, when, null);
            if (b.isPresent()) return b.get();
        }
        throw new SchedulingException("no room for " + attendees + " people at " + when.start().toLocalTime());
    }

    /** A specific room, or a clear error. */
    Booking bookRoom(String roomId, String organizer, String title, Interval when) {
        return tryBook(roomId, organizer, title, when, null)
                .orElseThrow(() -> new SchedulingException(roomId + " is busy at " + when.start().toLocalTime()));
    }

    /** Every occurrence or none: all checks and inserts happen under the room's lock. */
    List<Booking> bookWeekly(String roomId, String organizer, String title, Interval first, int weeks) {
        RoomCalendar cal = calendar(roomId);
        List<Interval> occurrences = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int w = 0; w < weeks; w++) occurrences.add(first.plus(Duration.ofDays(7L * w)));
        String series = "S" + seriesIds.getAndIncrement();
        cal.lock.lock();
        try {
            for (Interval i : occurrences)
                if (!cal.isFree(i)) throw new SchedulingException(roomId + " is busy on " + i.start().toLocalDate() + "; nothing booked");
            List<Booking> out = new ArrayList<>();
            for (Interval i : occurrences) out.add(insert(cal, organizer, title, i, series));
            return out;
        } finally {
            cal.lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    void cancel(String bookingId) {
        Booking b = bookings.remove(bookingId);
        if (b == null) throw new SchedulingException("no booking " + bookingId);
        RoomCalendar cal = calendar(b.roomId());
        cal.lock.lock();
        try { cal.remove(b); } finally { cal.lock.unlock(); }
    }

    /** Rooms free for the whole interval with enough seats. A snapshot: booking may still lose a race. */
    List<String> freeRooms(Interval when, int attendees) {
        List<String> out = new ArrayList<>();
        for (RoomCalendar cal : calendars.values()) {
            if (cal.room.capacity() < attendees) continue;
            cal.lock.lock();
            try { if (cal.isFree(when)) out.add(cal.room.id()); } finally { cal.lock.unlock(); }
        }
        return out;
    }

    List<Booking> bookingsFor(String roomId) {
        RoomCalendar cal = calendar(roomId);
        cal.lock.lock();
        try { return cal.all(); } finally { cal.lock.unlock(); }
    }

    private Optional<Booking> tryBook(String roomId, String organizer, String title, Interval when, String series) {
        RoomCalendar cal = calendar(roomId);
        cal.lock.lock();
        try {
            if (!cal.isFree(when)) return Optional.empty();
            return Optional.of(insert(cal, organizer, title, when, series));
        } finally {
            cal.lock.unlock();
        }
    }

    private Booking insert(RoomCalendar cal, String organizer, String title, Interval when, String series) {
        Booking b = new Booking("B" + ids.getAndIncrement(), cal.room.id(), organizer, title, when, series);
        cal.add(b);
        bookings.put(b.id(), b);
        return b;
    }

    private RoomCalendar calendar(String roomId) {
        RoomCalendar c = calendars.get(roomId);
        if (c == null) throw new SchedulingException("no room " + roomId);
        return c;
    }
}

    import java.util.List;

/** Orders the rooms worth trying for a meeting; the service does the atomic booking. */
interface RoomSelectionStrategy {
    List<Room> candidates(List<Room> rooms, int attendees);
}
    SmallestFittingRoom.java
    import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

/** Big rooms stay free for big meetings: try the smallest room that fits first. */
class SmallestFittingRoom implements RoomSelectionStrategy {
    public List<Room> candidates(List<Room> rooms, int attendees) {
        return rooms.stream()
                .filter(r -> r.capacity() >= attendees)
                .sorted(Comparator.comparingInt(Room::capacity).thenComparing(Room::id))
                .toList();
    }
}

    Demo.java (complete)
    public class Demo {
    static final LocalDateTime MON = LocalDateTime.of(2026, 10, 26, 0, 0);

    static Interval at(int day, int h1, int m1, int h2, int m2) {
        return new Interval(MON.plusDays(day).withHour(h1).withMinute(m1), MON.plusDays(day).withHour(h2).withMinute(m2));
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        SchedulerService s = new SchedulerService(
                List.of(new Room("R1", 4), new Room("R2", 8), new Room("R3", 20)), new SmallestFittingRoom());
        Booking a = s.book("asha", "design review", 6, at(0, 10, 0, 11, 0));     // R1 too small: R2
        Booking b = s.book("ravi", "sprint plan", 6, at(0, 10, 30, 11, 30));     // R2 busy: R3
        Booking c = s.book("meera", "1:1", 2, at(0, 11, 0, 12, 0));              // R1, touching is fine
        System.out.println(a.roomId() + " " + b.roomId() + " " + c.roomId());
        try { s.bookRoom("R2", "kabir", "sync", at(0, 10, 45, 11, 15)); }
        catch (SchedulingException e) { System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }

        List<Booking> standups = s.bookWeekly("R1", "team", "standup", at(0, 9, 0, 9, 15), 4);
        System.out.println("weekly standup: " + standups.size() + " occurrences, series " + standups.get(0).seriesId());
        try { s.bookWeekly("R1", "team", "retro", at(0, 11, 30, 12, 30), 3); }      // week 1 clashes with the 1:1
        catch (SchedulingException e) { System.out.println("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }
        System.out.println("R1 bookings: " + s.bookingsFor("R1").size() + " (the retro added none)");

        System.out.println("free for 3 people at 10:15: " + s.freeRooms(at(0, 10, 15, 10, 45), 3));
        s.cancel(a.id());
        System.out.println("after cancelling " + a.id() + ": " + s.freeRooms(at(0, 10, 15, 10, 45), 3));
        check(a.roomId().equals("R2") && b.roomId().equals("R3") && c.roomId().equals("R1"), "rooms");
        check(s.bookingsFor("R1").size() == 5, "all or nothing");

        // 16 threads, 2,000 random 30-60 minute requests for R2 on one day: no two bookings overlap
        SchedulerService busy = new SchedulerService(List.of(new Room("R2", 8)), new SmallestFittingRoom());
        AtomicInteger booked = new AtomicInteger();
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(16);
        for (int t = 0; t < 16; t++) pool.submit(() -> {
            ThreadLocalRandom r = ThreadLocalRandom.current();
            for (int i = 0; i < 125; i++) {
                int startMin = 8 * 60 + r.nextInt(10 * 60);
                LocalDateTime st = MON.plusMinutes(startMin);
                try { busy.bookRoom("R2", "u", "m", new Interval(st, st.plusMinutes(30 + r.nextInt(31)))); booked.incrementAndGet(); }
                catch (SchedulingException ignored) { }
            }
        });
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "finished");
        List<Booking> all = busy.bookingsFor("R2");
        for (int i = 1; i < all.size(); i++)
            check(!all.get(i - 1).interval().overlaps(all.get(i).interval()), "overlap");
        System.out.println("2,000 concurrent requests for one room: every accepted booking is free of overlaps");
        check(booked.get() == all.size(), "count");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P14.6Concurrency

    Race Defense
    Two people book overlapping slots in one room Check and insert under that room's lock; the second sees the first's booking
    Auto-pick races for the last free room Each candidate is tried atomically; a loser moves to the next candidate, like parking spots in P1
    A series half-booked by a concurrent request The series checks every date and inserts every date under one hold of the room's lock
    "Free rooms" answer goes stale It is a snapshot; booking re-checks under the lock and may still fail, which the UI must handle

    Locks are per room, so bookings in different rooms never wait for each other. A booking never needs two rooms' locks at once, so there is no lock ordering to get wrong; if a meeting ever needs two rooms together, take their locks in room-ID order (Module 9).

    In production

    In a database, the same rule is an exclusion constraint. PostgreSQL can enforce "no two bookings in one room overlap" directly: EXCLUDE USING gist (room_id WITH =, tsrange(start_at, end_at) WITH &&) (the btree_gist extension lets the equality on room ID sit in the same index). Two concurrent inserts that overlap cannot both commit, which is the database doing what the room lock does here.

    P14.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      Find the earliest common free slot

      Five people and a room must all be free for 30 minutes this week.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Merge everyone's busy intervals (sort by start, merge overlaps), including the room's bookings, then walk the gaps between merged intervals within working hours and take the first gap of at least 30 minutes. O(k log k) for k busy intervals.

    2. 2
      Time zones and daylight saving

      The series is "every Monday at 9:00 in Bengaluru" and some attendees are in London.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Store each occurrence as a zoned time in the organizer's zone (ZonedDateTime with the zone ID), generate recurrences in that zone so "9:00 local" stays 9:00 across daylight-saving changes, and convert to each viewer's zone only for display. Adding 7 x 24 hours to an instant drifts by an hour when the clocks change.

    3. 3
      Cancel one occurrence, or the rest of a series

      How do you model exceptions to a recurring rule?

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Each occurrence is a booking with the series ID, so cancelling one is cancelling that booking. "This and following" cancels occurrences with the series ID and a start at or after the chosen one. Calendar products store the rule (RRULE) plus exceptions instead of expanding forever; expanding a bounded horizon (say a year) is the simple interview answer.

    4. 4
      Room features

      Some meetings need a video unit or a whiteboard.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Give Room a set of features and filter candidates by the requested features in the selection strategy. A different strategy can prefer the room closest to the organizer's floor. Selection stays pluggable; the booking logic does not change.

    Minutes Do

    8-20 Interval with tests for overlap edges (touching, nested, identical)
    20-40 RoomCalendar with TreeMap, isFree, add, remove

    P14.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: half-open intervals; O(log n) overlap check with a sorted map; per-room atomic booking; selection strategy; cancellation.
    • Above the bar: all-or-nothing series; snapshot vs booking explained; time-zone-correct recurrence; the earliest common slot; the database exclusion constraint.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why are intervals half-open?
      Reveal

      So back-to-back meetings (10:00-11:00 and 11:00-12:00) do not clash, and the overlap test stays one rule: a.start < b.end && b.start < a.end.

    2. Why check only the floor and ceiling entries?
      Reveal

      Bookings in one room never overlap, so sorted by start they are also sorted by end. Any booking that starts before the floor ends before the floor starts, and any booking after the ceiling starts after it, so neither can reach the new interval.

    3. Why a lock per room rather than per service?
      Reveal

      A booking only touches one room's calendar, so different rooms are independent. A service-wide lock would make every booking in the building wait for every other.

    4. Why does "smallest room that fits" matter?
      Reveal

      Without it, a two-person meeting can take the 20-seat room and leave a large meeting with nowhere to go. A selection strategy encodes that policy and can be swapped.

    Problem 15: Food delivery order lifecycle

    Swiggy and Zomato in LLD form. The heart is an order state machine where every move names the actor allowed to make it (restaurant, customer, or the assigned partner), with cancellation refunds that depend on how far the order got. Around it: a bill frozen at placement, partner assignment that never gives one partner two orders, observers that update every app, and the race between "restaurant accepts" and "customer cancels".

    Try it first60 minutes

    Design the order flow of a food delivery app: place an order, the restaurant accepts or rejects, prepares, marks ready; a delivery partner is assigned, picks up, delivers; the customer can cancel for a refund that depends on timing; every party sees status changes. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: Order with a status changed only through one move(to, actor, actorId) that checks a transition table naming the actor for each move; a Bill computed once at placement with prices captured in the order items; a CancellationPolicy strategy for refunds by status; partner assignment by an AssignmentStrategy with an atomic claim on each partner, and a waiting queue when none is free; listeners notified after each move; and an explanation of the accept-versus-cancel race and how the order's lock decides it.

    P15.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Who acts? Customer places and cancels; restaurant accepts, rejects, prepares, marks ready; the assigned partner picks up and delivers
    Cancellation? Full refund before the restaurant accepts, half after; none once cooking starts
    Bill? Items plus 5% GST; delivery free from 499 rupees, else 30 rupees
    Partner assignment? When the restaurant accepts, the nearest free partner; if none, wait for the next free one
    Notifications? Customer, restaurant, and partner apps see every status change
    Out of scope Payments, ratings, live tracking, batching two orders per partner (follow-ups)

    Invariants: status changes only along the table, by the actor the table names; only the assigned partner can pick up and deliver; a partner holds at most one live order; prices on an order never change after placement; a refund is computed once, from the status the order was cancelled from.

    OrderStatus.java: the moves and their actors as data
    enum OrderStatus {
    PLACED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PREPARING, READY, PICKED_UP, DELIVERED, CANCELLED;

    /** from -> (to -> the only actor allowed to make that move). The state diagram as data. */
    private static final Map<OrderStatus, Map<OrderStatus, Actor>> MOVES = new EnumMap<>(OrderStatus.class);

    private static void allow(OrderStatus from, OrderStatus to, Actor who) {
        MOVES.computeIfAbsent(from, k -> new EnumMap<>(OrderStatus.class)).put(to, who);
    }

    static {
        allow(PLACED, ACCEPTED, Actor.RESTAURANT);
        allow(PLACED, REJECTED, Actor.RESTAURANT);
        allow(PLACED, CANCELLED, Actor.CUSTOMER);
        allow(ACCEPTED, PREPARING, Actor.RESTAURANT);
        allow(ACCEPTED, CANCELLED, Actor.CUSTOMER);
        allow(PREPARING, READY, Actor.RESTAURANT);
        allow(READY, PICKED_UP, Actor.PARTNER);
        allow(PICKED_UP, DELIVERED, Actor.PARTNER);
    }

    /** The actor allowed to move from this status to `to`, or null if the move does not exist. */
    Actor actorFor(OrderStatus to) { return MOVES.getOrDefault(this, Map.of()).get(to); }
}
    Order.java: one guarded move method
    class Order {
    final String id, customerId, restaurantId;
    final List<OrderItem> items;
    final Bill bill;
    private OrderStatus status = OrderStatus.PLACED;   // guarded by this
    private String partnerId;                          // guarded by this

    Order(String id, String customerId, String restaurantId, List<OrderItem> items) {
        if (items.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalArgumentException("empty order");
        this.id = id; this.customerId = customerId; this.restaurantId = restaurantId;
        this.items = List.copyOf(items);
        this.bill = Bill.of(this.items);
    }

    /** One synchronized check-and-set: the move must exist, the actor must own it, and the partner must match. */
    synchronized OrderEvent move(OrderStatus to, Actor actor, String actorId) {
        Actor allowed = status.actorFor(to);
        if (allowed == null) throw new IllegalStateException("order " + id + " cannot go from " + status + " to " + to);
        if (allowed != actor) throw new IllegalStateException(actor + " cannot move order " + id + " to " + to);
        if (actor == Actor.PARTNER && !actorId.equals(partnerId)) throw new IllegalStateException(actorId + " is not assigned to " + id);
        OrderStatus from = status;
        status = to;
        return new OrderEvent(id, from, to, actor + " " + actorId);
    }

    /** False if the order no longer needs a partner (cancelled meanwhile, or already has one). */
    synchronized boolean assign(String partnerId) {
        if (status != OrderStatus.ACCEPTED || this.partnerId != null) return false;
        this.partnerId = partnerId;
        return true;
    }

    synchronized OrderStatus status() { return status; }
    synchronized String partnerId() { return partnerId; }
}
    OrderService.java: place, accept, advance, cancel, assign
    class OrderService {
    private final Map<String, Order> orders = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final Map<String, Location> restaurants = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
    private final List<DeliveryPartner> partners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    private final Queue<String> waitingForPartner = new ConcurrentLinkedQueue<>();
    private final List<OrderListener> listeners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
    private final AssignmentStrategy assignment;
    private final CancellationPolicy cancellation;
    private final AtomicLong ids = new AtomicLong(1);

    OrderService(AssignmentStrategy assignment, CancellationPolicy cancellation) {
        this.assignment = assignment;
        this.cancellation = cancellation;
    }

    void addRestaurant(String id, Location at) { restaurants.put(id, at); }
    void addPartner(DeliveryPartner p) { partners.add(p); }
    void subscribe(OrderListener l) { listeners.add(l); }

    Order place(String customerId, String restaurantId, List<OrderItem> items) {
        if (!restaurants.containsKey(restaurantId)) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no restaurant " + restaurantId);
        Order o = new Order("O" + ids.getAndIncrement(), customerId, restaurantId, items);
        orders.put(o.id, o);
        publish(new OrderEvent(o.id, null, OrderStatus.PLACED, "total " + o.bill.totalPaise()));
        return o;
    }

    /** The restaurant accepts; a partner is assigned now so they arrive while the food is cooked. */
    void accept(String orderId, String restaurantId) {
        Order o = order(orderId);
        if (!o.restaurantId.equals(restaurantId)) throw new IllegalStateException(restaurantId + " does not own " + orderId);
        publish(o.move(OrderStatus.ACCEPTED, Actor.RESTAURANT, restaurantId));
        if (!tryAssign(o)) waitingForPartner.add(o.id);              // assigned later, when a partner frees up
    }

    void advance(String orderId, OrderStatus to, Actor actor, String actorId) {
        Order o = order(orderId);
        publish(o.move(to, actor, actorId));
        if (to == OrderStatus.DELIVERED) partnerFree(partner(actorId));
    }

    /** Returns the refund; the same move check stops a cancel that races with acceptance or cooking. */
    long cancel(String orderId, String customerId) {
        Order o = order(orderId);
        if (!o.customerId.equals(customerId)) throw new IllegalStateException(customerId + " does not own " + orderId);
        OrderEvent e = o.move(OrderStatus.CANCELLED, Actor.CUSTOMER, customerId);
        long refund = cancellation.refundPaise(e.from(), o.bill);
        String p = o.partnerId();
        if (p != null) partnerFree(partner(p));
        publish(new OrderEvent(e.orderId(), e.from(), e.to(), "refund " + refund));
        return refund;
    }

    /** True when the order is settled: it got a partner, or it was cancelled and needs none. */
    private boolean tryAssign(Order o) {
        for (DeliveryPartner p : assignment.candidates(partners, restaurants.get(o.restaurantId))) {
            if (!p.tryClaim()) continue;                               // atomic: no partner gets two orders
            if (o.assign(p.id)) {
                publish(new OrderEvent(o.id, OrderStatus.ACCEPTED, OrderStatus.ACCEPTED, "partner " + p.id));
            } else {
                p.release();                                           // cancelled meanwhile: give the partner back
            }
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    private void partnerFree(DeliveryPartner p) {
        p.release();
        for (String id; (id = waitingForPartner.poll()) != null; ) {   // hand the partner to a waiting order
            Order w = orders.get(id);
            if (w.status() != OrderStatus.ACCEPTED) continue;          // cancelled while waiting
            if (!tryAssign(w)) waitingForPartner.add(id);              // someone else took the partner first
            return;
        }
    }

    private void publish(OrderEvent e) {                              // called outside order locks
        for (OrderListener l : listeners) {
            try { l.onEvent(e); } catch (RuntimeException ignored) { /* a failing listener never blocks an order */ }
        }
    }

    Order order(String id) {
        Order o = orders.get(id);
        if (o == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("no order " + id);
        return o;
    }

    private DeliveryPartner partner(String id) {
        return partners.stream().filter(p -> p.id.equals(id)).findFirst()
                .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException("no partner " + id));
    }

    int waiting() { return waitingForPartner.size(); }
}
    DeliveryPartner.java: an atomic claim
    class DeliveryPartner {
    final String id;
    volatile Location location;
    private final AtomicBoolean free = new AtomicBoolean(true);

    DeliveryPartner(String id, Location location) { this.id = id; this.location = location; }

    /** Compare-and-set: of many orders racing for this partner, exactly one wins. */
    boolean tryClaim() { return free.compareAndSet(true, false); }
    void release() { free.set(true); }
    boolean isFree() { return free.get(); }
}
    Bill.java
    record Bill(long itemsPaise, long taxPaise, long deliveryFeePaise, long totalPaise) {
    static final long FREE_DELIVERY_FROM = 49_900;   // orders of 499 rupees or more

    static Bill of(List<OrderItem> items) {
        long subtotal = items.stream().mapToLong(OrderItem::totalPaise).sum();
        long tax = (subtotal * 5 + 50) / 100;                      // 5% GST on restaurant food, rounded half up
        long fee = subtotal >= FREE_DELIVERY_FROM ? 0 : 3_000;
        return new Bill(subtotal, tax, fee, subtotal + tax + fee);
    }
}

/** Orders the partners worth offering a pickup to; the service claims one atomically. */
interface AssignmentStrategy {

    NearestPartner.java
    import java.util.Comparator;
import java.util.List;

class NearestPartner implements AssignmentStrategy {
    public List<DeliveryPartner> candidates(List<DeliveryPartner> partners, Location restaurant) {
        return partners.stream()
                .filter(DeliveryPartner::isFree)
                .sorted(Comparator.comparingDouble((DeliveryPartner p) -> p.location.distanceTo(restaurant)).thenComparing(p -> p.id))
                .toList();
    }
}
    CancellationPolicy.java
    /** How much of the bill a cancellation refunds, by the status it is cancelled from. */
interface CancellationPolicy {
    long refundPaise(OrderStatus from, Bill bill);
}
    StandardCancellation.java
    class StandardCancellation implements CancellationPolicy {
    public long refundPaise(OrderStatus from, Bill bill) {
        return switch (from) {
            case PLACED -> bill.totalPaise();          // the restaurant has not started: full refund
            case ACCEPTED -> bill.totalPaise() / 2;    // the restaurant committed: half
            default -> throw new IllegalStateException("cannot refund a cancellation from " + from);
        };
    }
}

    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        OrderService svc = new OrderService(new NearestPartner(), new StandardCancellation());
        svc.addRestaurant("R1", new Location(0, 0));
        svc.addPartner(new DeliveryPartner("D1", new Location(5, 5)));
        svc.addPartner(new DeliveryPartner("D2", new Location(1, 1)));
        List<String> feed = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
        svc.subscribe(e -> feed.add(e.orderId() + " " + (e.from() == e.to() ? "" : e.to() + " ") + "(" + e.detail() + ")"));

        Order o1 = svc.place("asha", "R1", List.of(new OrderItem("biryani", 2, 25_000), new OrderItem("cola", 1, 4_000)));
        svc.accept(o1.id, "R1");                                           // D2 is nearer: assigned
        svc.advance(o1.id, OrderStatus.PREPARING, Actor.RESTAURANT, "R1");
        try { svc.cancel(o1.id, "asha"); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { feed.add("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }
        svc.advance(o1.id, OrderStatus.READY, Actor.RESTAURANT, "R1");
        try { svc.advance(o1.id, OrderStatus.PICKED_UP, Actor.PARTNER, "D1"); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { feed.add("rejected: " + e.getMessage()); }
        svc.advance(o1.id, OrderStatus.PICKED_UP, Actor.PARTNER, "D2");
        svc.advance(o1.id, OrderStatus.DELIVERED, Actor.PARTNER, "D2");

        Order o2 = svc.place("ravi", "R1", List.of(new OrderItem("dosa", 1, 12_000)));
        long refund = svc.cancel(o2.id, "ravi");                           // before acceptance: full refund
        feed.forEach(System.out::println);
        System.out.println("O1 bill: " + o1.bill + "; O2 refund " + refund);
        check(o1.bill.totalPaise() == 56_700 && refund == o2.bill.totalPaise(), "bill and refund");

        // 200 orders, 5 partners; for each order the restaurant accepts while the customer cancels, at the same moment
        OrderService race = new OrderService(new NearestPartner(), new StandardCancellation());
        race.addRestaurant("R1", new Location(0, 0));
        List<DeliveryPartner> fleet = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { DeliveryPartner p = new DeliveryPartner("P" + i, new Location(i, i)); fleet.add(p); race.addPartner(p); }
        List<Order> made = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < 200; i++) made.add(race.place("c" + i, "R1", List.of(new OrderItem("thali", 1, 20_000))));
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
        CountDownLatch go = new CountDownLatch(1);
        for (Order o : made) {
            pool.submit(() -> { await(go); try { race.accept(o.id, "R1"); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { } });
            pool.submit(() -> { await(go); try { race.cancel(o.id, o.customerId); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { } });
        }
        go.countDown();
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "finished");
        Set<String> holders = ConcurrentHashMap.newKeySet();
        for (Order o : made) {
            check(o.status() == OrderStatus.ACCEPTED || o.status() == OrderStatus.CANCELLED, "one end state");
            if (o.status() == OrderStatus.ACCEPTED && o.partnerId() != null) check(holders.add(o.partnerId()), "partner on two live orders");
        }
        long busy = fleet.stream().filter(p -> !p.isFree()).count();
        check(busy == holders.size(), "a busy partner without a live order (leaked claim)");
        System.out.println("accept vs cancel on 200 orders: each ended ACCEPTED or CANCELLED; every busy partner holds exactly one live order");
    }

    static void await(CountDownLatch l) { try { l.await(); } catch (InterruptedException e) { Thread.currentThread().interrupt(); } }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}

    P15.6Concurrency

    Race Defense
    Restaurant accepts while the customer cancels Both go through Order.move, which is synchronized; the second sees the first's status and either fails or takes the legal path (cancel after accept, half refund)
    Two orders claim the same partner DeliveryPartner.tryClaim is a compare-and-set on the free flag; one wins
    A partner claimed for an order cancelled a moment earlier Order.assign succeeds only while the order is still ACCEPTED, under the order's lock; otherwise the partner is released at once
    A freed partner and a waiting order The service hands the freed partner to the oldest waiting order; if another order claims the partner first, the waiting order goes back in the queue
    A slow or failing app notification Listeners run after the move, outside the order's lock, each in its own try/catch
    Watch out

    The leak to look for in any assignment design: a resource (partner, seat, locker) claimed for an entity that changed state in between. Check the entity's state under its own lock at the moment of attaching the resource, and give the resource back if the check fails. The demo's final check, "every busy partner holds exactly one live order", exists to catch exactly that leak.

    In production

    Real delivery platforms run each step as a separate service talking through events: the order service owns the state machine, a dispatch service offers the order to partners (who may decline, so assignment is a short negotiation with timeouts), and notifications are consumers of order events on a queue. The rules are the same: one owner per state, conditional updates (UPDATE orders SET status = 'ACCEPTED' WHERE id = ? AND status = 'PLACED'), and idempotent consumers.

    P15.7Deep dives

    Guided designExtensions interviewers ask forAnswer each before revealing
    1. 1
      A partner can decline

      Assignment becomes an offer: the partner has 30 seconds to accept.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      Add an OFFERED step between free and assigned: claim the partner, send the offer, start a timer (P12). Accept attaches the partner to the order; decline or timeout releases the partner and offers the next candidate. The order records who declined so it is not offered to them again.

    2. 2
      Coupons and offers

      "FLAT100 on orders above 399", "20% up to 120 for new users".

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A chain of discount rules applied to the bill at placement (Module 6): each rule checks eligibility and returns a discount; the order stores which rule applied and the amount. Rules that cannot combine are marked exclusive; the pipeline picks the best eligible one. Capture the discount in the bill so a later rule change does not alter placed orders.

    3. 3
      Restaurant runs out of an item after accepting

      The kitchen cannot make one dish.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      A partial-fulfilment flow: the restaurant proposes a modified order, the customer accepts (bill recomputed, difference refunded) or cancels with a full refund because the failure is the restaurant's. Model it as a new state (AWAITING_CUSTOMER) with its own actor rules rather than an exception.

    4. 4
      Batch two orders for one partner

      Two orders from the same restaurant to nearby customers.

      Write your answer, then reveal

      The partner's capacity becomes 2 instead of a boolean: an atomic counter with compare-and-set up to the limit, and the assignment strategy prefers partners already heading to the same restaurant. Pickups and deliveries become per order; the partner is released when the counter returns to zero.

    P15.9What a strong answer shows

    • SDE-2 bar: a transition table with actor checks; captured prices and a bill computed once; cancellation policy by status; atomic partner claims; listeners after the change.
    • Above the bar: the cancel-during-assignment leak found and closed; a waiting queue for partners; offers with timeouts; the event-driven production version.
    Follow-up questionsPractice saying the answer out loud
    1. Why put the actor in the transition table instead of checking roles in each method?
      Reveal

      One table answers both questions, "is this move legal" and "who may make it", for every move. Adding a state or changing who may cancel is a data change in one place, and no method can forget the check.

    2. Why does OrderItem store the price?
      Reveal

      Menu prices change. The order must keep what the customer agreed to pay, so the bill and any refund are computed from captured prices, never from the live menu.

    3. Two threads call accept and cancel on the same order at the same instant. What are the possible outcomes?
      Reveal

      Accept first: the order is ACCEPTED, then the cancel succeeds from ACCEPTED with a half refund (and frees any partner). Cancel first: the order is CANCELLED with a full refund, and accept fails because CANCELLED has no move to ACCEPTED. Never both effects mixed.

    4. Why notify listeners outside the order's lock?
      Reveal

      Notifications can be slow or fail. Holding the order's lock during them would block the next move (the partner's pickup), and a failure must not undo a move that already happened.

    Problem 16: In-memory key-value store with transactions

    The "in-memory database" question, popular in machine coding rounds because it grows in stages: GET and SET, then nested BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK, then TTL, then many clients at once. The design that survives every stage keeps uncommitted writes in a stack of layers per session, applies a whole transaction to the shared store in one step, and uses versions so two clients never silently overwrite each other.

    Uses: M7 undo, M9 optimistic versions, M9 locks, M10 driver

    Try it first45 minutes

    Design an in-memory key-value store: get, put, delete; nested transactions with begin, commit, rollback (rollback undoes only the innermost level); keys with an optional time to live; many clients using it concurrently. Then compare.

    Reveal the answer

    Strong answer: a shared Store of committed entries (value, version, expiry) behind a read-write lock; a Session per client holding a stack of layers of pending writes, where a read checks layers innermost first and then the store; inner commit merges a layer into its parent, rollback drops it, and only the outermost commit reaches the store, all at once; deletes recorded as tombstones in layers; lazy expiry on read plus a periodic purge; and for concurrency, versions recorded when a transaction first touches a key and checked at commit, so the second of two conflicting commits fails and retries.

    P16.1Requirements

    Question Assumed answer
    Operations? get, put (with optional TTL), delete
    Transactions? begin, commit, rollback; nestable; rollback and commit act on the innermost open level
    Visibility? A client sees its own uncommitted writes; other clients see only committed data
    Outside a transaction? Each write commits immediately
    TTL? An expired key reads as absent; memory is reclaimed later
    Concurrency? Many clients; two transactions writing the same key must not both "win" silently
    Out of scope Persistence, replication, eviction by memory size (deep dives)

    Invariants: the store changes only by whole outermost transactions (all writes or none); an inner rollback leaves outer levels untouched; nothing uncommitted is visible to other clients; a commit fails if any key it touched changed since it first touched it.

    P16.2Entities and responsibilities

    Class Responsibility
    Store Committed entries with versions and expiry; read; atomic commit(writes, seen); purgeExpired
    Entry (record) Value, version, expiry time
    Session One client's stack of open transactions; read-your-writes; begin, commit, rollback
    Write (record) A pending value with TTL, or the DELETE tombstone
    ConflictException Another commit won; the caller retries from begin

    Session.java: layers of pending writes
    /** One client's view: a stack of open transactions over the shared store. Not shared between threads. */
class Session {
    private final Store store;
    private final Deque<Map<String, Write>> layers = new ArrayDeque<>();   // pending writes per BEGIN; top = innermost
    private final Map<String, Long> seen = new HashMap<>();                // store version of each key the transaction touched

    Session(Store store) { this.store = store; }

    Optional<String> get(String key) {
        for (Map<String, Write> layer : layers) {                          // innermost first
            Write w = layer.get(key);
            if (w != null) return w.isDelete() ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(w.value());
        }
        remember(key);
        return store.read(key).map(Entry::value);
    }

    void put(String key, String value) { write(key, new Write(value, 0)); }
    void put(String key, String value, long ttlMillis) { write(key, new Write(value, ttlMillis)); }
    void delete(String key) { write(key, Write.DELETE); }

    void begin() {
        if (layers.isEmpty()) seen.clear();                                 // a new outermost transaction
        layers.push(new LinkedHashMap<>());
    }

    /** Inner commit merges into the parent; the outermost commit applies everything to the store at once. */
    void commit() {
        Map<String, Write> top = pop("COMMIT");
        if (!layers.isEmpty()) {
            layers.peek().putAll(top);
            return;
        }
        try {
            store.commit(top, seen);                                       // may throw ConflictException: the work is discarded
        } finally {
            seen.clear();
        }
    }

    void rollback() {                                                      // drops the innermost level only
        pop("ROLLBACK");
        if (layers.isEmpty()) seen.clear();
    }

    int depth() { return layers.size(); }

    private void write(String key, Write w) {
        if (layers.isEmpty()) {                                            // no transaction: a one-write commit
            store.commit(Map.of(key, w), Map.of());
            return;
        }
        remember(key);
        layers.peek().put(key, w);
    }

    /** The first time a transaction touches a key, record the version it saw; commit checks it is unchanged. */
    private void remember(String key) {
        if (!layers.isEmpty()) seen.computeIfAbsent(key, store::versionOf);
    }

    private Map<String, Write> pop(String what) {
        if (layers.isEmpty()) throw new IllegalStateException(what + " with no open transaction");
        return layers.pop();
    }
}
    Store.java: atomic, versioned commit
    /** Shared committed data. Many readers at once; commits are exclusive and all-or-nothing. */
class Store {
    private final Map<String, Entry> data = new HashMap<>();            // guarded by rw
    private final ReentrantReadWriteLock rw = new ReentrantReadWriteLock();
    private final LongSupplier clock;
    private long nextVersion = 1;                                        // guarded by the write lock

    Store(LongSupplier clock) { this.clock = clock; }

    /** The live entry, if any. An expired entry reads as absent (lazy expiry). */
    Optional<Entry> read(String key) {
        rw.readLock().lock();
        try {
            Entry e = data.get(key);
            return e != null && e.isLive(clock.getAsLong()) ? Optional.of(e) : Optional.empty();
        } finally {
            rw.readLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    /** Version a transaction saw for a key: 0 if absent or expired. */
    long versionOf(String key) { return read(key).map(Entry::version).orElse(0L); }

    /**
     * Applies all writes, or none: if any key's version changed since the transaction first touched it,
     * another commit won, and this one fails (first committer wins, so no update is lost).
     */
    void commit(Map<String, Write> writes, Map<String, Long> seen) {
        rw.writeLock().lock();
        try {
            long now = clock.getAsLong();
            for (Map.Entry<String, Long> s : seen.entrySet()) {
                Entry cur = data.get(s.getKey());
                long v = cur != null && cur.isLive(now) ? cur.version() : 0;
                if (v != s.getValue()) throw new ConflictException("key " + s.getKey() + " changed after this transaction first touched it");
            }
            for (Map.Entry<String, Write> w : writes.entrySet()) {
                Write x = w.getValue();
                if (x.isDelete()) data.remove(w.getKey());
                else data.put(w.getKey(), new Entry(x.value(), nextVersion++, x.ttlMillis() > 0 ? now + x.ttlMillis() : 0));
            }
        } finally {
            rw.writeLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    /** Removes expired entries; run it on a timer to free memory. Reads never depend on it. */
    int purgeExpired() {
        rw.writeLock().lock();
        try {
            long now = clock.getAsLong();
            int before = data.size();
            data.values().removeIf(e -> !e.isLive(now));
            return before - data.size();
        } finally {
            rw.writeLock().unlock();
        }
    }

    int size() {
        rw.readLock().lock();
        try { return data.size(); } finally { rw.readLock().unlock(); }
    }
}

    Entry.java
    /** A stored value. `version` grows on every committed write; expiresAt is 0 for no expiry. */
record Entry(String value, long version, long expiresAt) {
    boolean isLive(long now) { return expiresAt == 0 || now < expiresAt; }
}
    Write.java
    /** One pending change in a transaction: a value with an optional TTL, or a delete (value == null). */
record Write(String value, long ttlMillis) {
    static final Write DELETE = new Write(null, 0);
    boolean isDelete() { return value == null; }
}

    // 8 threads x 500 increments of one counter, each in a transaction retried on conflict
new Session(store).put("hits", "0");
AtomicInteger retries = new AtomicInteger();
ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) pool.submit(() -> {
    Session c = new Session(store);
    for (int i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
        while (true) {
            c.begin();
            int v = Integer.parseInt(c.get("hits").orElse("0"));
            c.put("hits", String.valueOf(v + 1));
            try { c.commit(); break; } catch (ConflictException e) { retries.incrementAndGet(); }
        }
    }
});

    public class Demo {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        AtomicLong now = new AtomicLong(1_000);                          // manual clock, in milliseconds
        Store store = new Store(now::get);
        List<String> out = new ArrayList<>();
        Session s = new Session(store);
        s.put("a", "10");
        s.begin();
        s.put("a", "20");
        s.begin();
        s.delete("a");
        out.add("inner sees a = " + s.get("a").orElse("(none)"));
        s.rollback();                                                    // undo only the delete
        out.add("after inner rollback a = " + s.get("a").orElse("(none)"));
        out.add("another client still sees a = " + new Session(store).get("a").orElse("(none)"));
        s.commit();                                                      // outermost commit: applied to the store
        out.add("after commit, another client sees a = " + new Session(store).get("a").orElse("(none)"));

        s.put("otp:asha", "4821", 30_000);                               // expires in 30 seconds
        now.addAndGet(31_000);
        out.add("otp after 31 s: " + s.get("otp:asha").orElse("(expired)") + "; purged " + store.purgeExpired());

        Session t1 = new Session(store), t2 = new Session(store);
        t1.begin(); t2.begin();
        t1.put("seat:A1", "ravi");
        t2.put("seat:A1", "meera");
        t1.commit();
        try { t2.commit(); } catch (ConflictException e) { out.add("t2: " + e.getMessage()); }
        out.add("seat:A1 = " + new Session(store).get("seat:A1").orElseThrow());
        out.forEach(System.out::println);
        check(new Session(store).get("a").orElseThrow().equals("20"), "commit");

        // 8 threads x 500 increments of one counter, each in a transaction retried on conflict
        new Session(store).put("hits", "0");
        AtomicInteger retries = new AtomicInteger();
        ExecutorService pool = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(8);
        for (int t = 0; t < 8; t++) pool.submit(() -> {
            Session c = new Session(store);
            for (int i = 0; i < 500; i++) {
                while (true) {
                    c.begin();
                    int v = Integer.parseInt(c.get("hits").orElse("0"));
                    c.put("hits", String.valueOf(v + 1));
                    try { c.commit(); break; } catch (ConflictException e) { retries.incrementAndGet(); }
                }
            }
        });
        pool.shutdown();
        check(pool.awaitTermination(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS), "finished");
        String hits = new Session(store).get("hits").orElseThrow();
        System.out.println("4,000 transactional increments from 8 threads: hits = " + hits + " (conflicts retried, none lost)");
        check(hits.equals("4000"), "no lost update");
    }

    static void check(boolean ok, String what) { if (!ok) throw new AssertionError(what); }
}
